categories.label: Art & Galleries
categories.description: Public and university galleries, artist-run studio groups, commercial galleries and print organisations. Exhibitions run for months rather than weeks, so most of this category is harvested monthly.

categories.label: Cinema
categories.description: Cork's multiplexes, its arthouse and independent screens, and the film societies and arts-centre cinemas that programme world cinema between festivals.

categories.label: City-wide
categories.description: Cross-category listings sites, ticketing platforms, the local news titles, the council and the universities. These are the safety net for a city whose programme is mostly pub sessions, one-off gigs in borrowed rooms and free community events that no venue website will ever list.

categories.label: Comedy
categories.description: Cork's two dedicated comedy clubs, the weekly stand-up and improv nights that run in rooms which are otherwise pubs and music venues, and the theatres that host touring comedy.

categories.label: Learning & Talks
categories.description: Public lectures, adult education and outreach — the programmes whose purpose is that someone leaves knowing something. The two universities carry most of it in Cork, and they belong here rather than among the city-wide aggregators: what they publish is a teaching programme, not a listings service.

categories.label: Family & Kids
categories.description: Wildlife and science attractions, young people's theatre, puppetry and circus, play centres, and the children's strands of the city libraries and the council's own programme. Cork's free family programme is largely civic — the council, the libraries and the two universities carry it — and it spikes at midterms, Cruinniú na nÓg in June and Halloween.

categories.label: Festivals
categories.description: Cork's year is festival-shaped, and most of it happens in borrowed rooms rather than at a venue that would list it. Jazz over the October bank holiday and Midsummer in June are the two peaks; Halloween, St Patrick's and Christmas are civic events run by the council; the film, folk, choral and craft festivals fill in the rest. Almost every entry here is silent between editions, which is why nearly all of them are quarterly.

categories.label: Food & Drink
categories.description: Food and drink events in Cork — festivals, tastings, supper clubs, cookery courses, brewery and distillery tours, food-tour operators. Only sources that actually programme events belong here; a restaurant with no public programme is not a source, however good it is. The English Market, Marina Market and the farmers' markets are deliberately left to the markets category rather than catalogued twice.

categories.label: Literature & Talks
categories.description: Cork's literature organisations and festivals, the city library service, bookshops that run launches and readings, university literary programmes, poetry and short-story nights, and public lecture societies.

categories.label: Making & Craft
categories.description:
Makerspaces, print and craft studios, pottery, textiles, woodwork, boat building, repair projects and the public course programmes of Cork's art college.
Two things shape this category in Cork. First, most of what these sources publish is a *course* rather than an event — a ten-week evening class is not a one-off workshop, and a "what's on" page fills up with enrolment listings if they are treated the same. Prefer one-off and short workshops, open days and public makes; record a recurring course as `occurrence.kind: recurring` with its pattern stated.
Second, the dates are usually on a booking platform rather than a listings page. Cork Craft & Design sells its whole programme as Shopify products with the date in the product title; Cork Printmakers publishes course subjects and no dates at all. Where a booking route is the only place real dates exist, it is recorded as a route here rather than left for stage 2 to discover.
The August peak is Cork Craft Month, and the April one is the Lifelong Learning Festival — between them they carry more hands-on making than the year-round programme does.

categories.label: Markets
categories.description: Cork's covered market and food halls, the weekly farmers' markets ringing the city, flea and craft markets, and the seasonal Christmas trading. Almost every entry is one `occurrence.kind: recurring` event with the day and time stated in prose — very few of these sources keep a diary at all.

categories.label: Museums & Heritage
categories.description: Civic and independent museums, forts, historic buildings, cathedrals and an observatory — plus the heritage societies and heritage-week platforms that programme into them. Mostly permanent collections (`occurrence.kind: ongoing`) with temporary exhibitions as `run` and tours or talks as `single`.

categories.label: Music
categories.description: Concert halls, songwriter rooms, converted churches, club and warehouse spaces, the docklands marquee season, the conservatoire, and the promoters and gig guides that carry what no single venue publishes. Cork's largest category.

categories.label: Parks, Gardens & Outdoors
categories.description: Parks and green space, gardens and arboretums, guided walking tours and the nature and outdoor-activity organisations that programme into all of them. Cork merges what Bristol splits between outdoors and gardens, because inside a 12km radius the city has almost no horticultural sites of its own — three gardens, one accredited arboretum, and a council estate of parks with no events diary anywhere in it.

categories.label: Sport
categories.description: Hurling and Gaelic football first — in Cork these are civic occasions, not a niche — then rugby, League of Ireland football, greyhound and horse racing, athletics, rowing on the Lee, and the free weekly participation events. Most of this is fixture lists: they are published a season at a time and then move, so the value is in re-checking dates rather than discovering new events.

categories.label: Theatre
categories.description: Main houses, studio theatres, university theatres, dance, circus and contemporary performance, and the companies that programme into other people's spaces.

categories.label: Trad & Folk
categories.description: Pub sessions, singers' clubs, Comhaltas branches, pipers and folk festivals — the weekly, unticketed, largely unadvertised music that Cork is best at.

events.title: TRISKEL SAMPLE Project Space: Billy Lingwood Residency & Exhibition

price.text: Admission is free and all are welcome

events.raw:
**TRISKEL SAMPLE Project Space: Billy Lingwood Residency &
Exhibition** — July 2 - August 30, 2026. TRISKEL SAMPLE Project Space
at Triskel Arts Centre. Admission free.
events.summary: Billy Lingwood's two-month residency in the project space Sample- Studios runs inside Triskel, ending with the work on show. Free, and in its last fortnight.
events.description:
Billy Lingwood is a Cork-based visual artist and arts worker with a BA in Fine Art: Printmaking & Contemporary Practice from LSAD. Their work explores post-colonial legacies in the Irish psyche and the social, cultural and policy impacts these continue to have on resident lifeforms. Rooted in printmaking, their practice often extends into curation, co-creation and intervention-based work.

In 2024, Billy was lead artist and project manager for Quilting the Rainbow, a Creative Ireland funded project celebrating over forty years of queer rights activism in Cork. That same year, they were awarded the Arts Council of Ireland's Artist in the Community R&D Award (managed by Create) to develop a future co-creation project with members of Cork's LGBTI+ community.

During the Triskel-Sample Project Space residency, Billy intends to further develop their practice within the field of co-creative arts participation. A key influence is the Art of Drag exhibition at De Hallen Haarlem (Netherlands), where the gallery supported a lead artist to establish a community group, run workshops in research and skills sharing and co-curate a multi-disciplinary exhibition with resources for hands-on public engagement. Drawing inspiration from this model, and following consultation with De Hallen's participation office, Billy is exploring how such an approach can be reimagined within a Cork context.

The residency will bring together a professional artist and a group of non-professional collaborators to investigate alternative models of community-based art making. Workshops will combine research, archival investigation, skill sharing and making.

events.title: Leanne McDonagh: Community & Connection
events.raw:
**Leanne McDonagh: Community & Connection** — 4th Jul - 12th Sep.
Sirius Arts Centre, Cobh. Wednesday - Saturday, 11.00 - 17:00.
events.summary: The fullest showing yet of Leanne McDonagh's photographs and prints of Traveller life, made from inside the community — family gatherings, trade, domestic interiors — with a new commission alongside work from 2011 to 2025. Curated by Sirius and touring on to Skibbereen and Limerick.
events.description:
Leanne McDonagh is an artist from the Traveller community based in
Cork County. She documents her community's life and heritage from an
insider perspective. Her work provides a nuanced and authentic
representation, challenging prevailing negative perceptions, attitudes
and beliefs by affirming Traveller identity in constructive ways.

McDonagh's practice encompasses photography and printmaking. Her
images portray family gatherings, celebrations, scenes of labour and
trade, domestic interiors and activities, and public meetings. They
subtly yet vividly capture the transient nature of the Traveller
community's circumstances, memories and experiences.

This exhibition constitutes the most comprehensive presentation of
McDonagh's work to date, featuring a newly commissioned series
alongside a broad selection spanning 2011 to 2025. It emphasises the
distinct characteristics of Traveller culture and examines both shared
and universal dimensions of social relations.

This exhibition is organised by SIRIUS and curated by Director Miguel
Amado. It is realised with funding from the Arts Council through a
Project Award. The presentation at SIRIUS is part of a tour including
Uillinn: West Cork Arts Centre and Limerick City Gallery of Art,
produced by Rayne Booth.

**Accessibility note:** there are three steps at the front entrance,
but a temporary wheelchair ramp is available upon request.

Installation project made in collaboration with Veronica Santorum and Benjamin Burns

Tuesday 4 August to Saturday 12 September

Monday 17 - Wednesday 19 August: 10am - 1pm

Thursday 20 - Friday 21 August: 10am - 5pm

Saturday 22 - Sunday 23 August: CLOSED

The Saérlaith Project is a new installation by Jools Gilson made in collaboration with visual artist Veronica Santorum and Sound Artist / Videographer Benjamin Burns.

Somewhere, there in the deep dark, I am wondering. I wonder with all this movement from before and from now and from what will come.

Rooms of whispering sphagnum moss, haunting dance films and 7th century bogstories. The Saérlaith Project digs deep into embodied audio with an art installation buried in Cloonshannagh Bog, Co. Roscommon. Bowls of sphagnum moss whisper, choreography collaborates with moths in short dance films, something moves beneath a haunted map; a real 7th Century female bog body has things to say.

Based on research conducted as part of an Arts Council Dance Bursary in 2023. Made with research support from Engineers Brendan O’Flynn and Colum Crowe (Tyndall Institute) and Dance Artist Justine Cooper. Funded by Insight (Research Ireland), The Arts Council, UCC and Fulbright Ireland.

events.description:
Triskel is delighted to partner with Crawford Art Gallery to present Artists Film International 2026 (AFI) under the theme *A Kind of Power*.

Bringing together artists and partner organisations from across the globe, this year's edition explores how systems of power shape the act of looking and the conditions under which we are seen.

This year Crawford Art Gallery selected artist Thaís Muniz to present her short film *The Kite Ballet.*

All films will be presented on a loop throughout the day. Free screenings, drop in, no booking required.

**Tue 11 - Thu 13 Aug / Tue 18 - Thu 20 Aug / Tue 25 - Thu 27 Aug, 10:00 – 15:30 each day.**

A public talk with **Thaís Muniz and Dr Eve Olney** with Dawn Williams, curator, Crawford Art Gallery, will take place on Thursday 27 August at 1pm.

**The full line-up includes:**

Razia Akbari, selected by Center for Contemporary Arts Afghanistan in eXiLe e.V. (CCAA in EXiLe), Frankfurt, Germany; Aqsa Arif, selected by Tramway, Glasgow, Scotland; Alessandra Ferrini, selected by Galleria d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea di Bergamo (GAMeC), Bergamo, Italy; Ira Goryainova, selected by argos centre for audiovisual arts, Brussels, Belgium; Kiyo Gutiérrez, selected by Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions (LACE), Los Angeles, USA; Marte Hodne Haugen, selected by Tromsø Kunstforening, Tromsø, Norway; Malik Irtiza, selected by Project 88, Mumbai, India; Thaís Muniz, selected by Crawford Art Gallery, Cork, Ireland; Ann Oren, selected by Video-Forum of Neuer Berliner Kunstverein (n.b.k), Berlin, Germany; Amaal Said, selected by Forma, London and Focal Point, Southend, UK; Mila Turajlić, selected by Cultural Centre of Belgrade, Belgrade, Serbia; Video News, selected by Sapieha Palace, branch of the Contemporary Art Centre (CAC), Vilnius, Lithuania.

Since the advent of cinema, moving image practice has been tied to questions of perception and power. Early filmmakers imagined the camera as a form of mechanical vision capable of revealing the world objectively, yet cinema quickly exposed how vision remains shaped by the social and political structures that organise the gaze. Throughout the twentieth century, colonial image-making, propaganda, ethnographic film, and patriarchal modes of spectatorship produced and reinforced regimes that shaped how people, cultures, and histories were seen and understood. Far from disappearing, today these systems of visibility have been reconfigured within contemporary digital image cultures defined by circulation, algorithmic mediation, surveillance infrastructures, and the relentless production of visual information.

*A Kind of Power* brings together a selection of international artists whose films renegotiate the fraught legacies of representation and respond to the conditions under which people, histories, and territories are made visible. Many of the artists move beyond critique alone, to explore how moving-image might create new forms of relation, attention, and collective presence. While some works confront contemporary systems of visibility directly, others propose alternative ways of inhabiting and understanding the world through ritual, memory, reciprocity, and acts of witnessing.

Image credit: Thaís Muniz, The Kite Ballet 2024 (detail). Photo: Antonello Veneri. Courtesy and © the Artist.

events.description:
**National Heritage Week at Nano Nagle Place** — 15th -22nd August | Cork City

Join us at Nano Nagle Place for a week of talks, workshops, performances, and
heritage events celebrating the stories, people, and traditions that have
shaped Cork's South Parish and beyond. As part of National Heritage Week 2026,
explore local history, genealogy, archives, art, and Gaeilge through a diverse
programme of events suitable for all interests!

**Programme Highlights**

- **€5 Self-Guided Tours of Nano Nagle Place Museum** — 15th-22nd August |
  Daily | Nano Nagle Place | €5 Entry. A special Heritage Week opportunity to
  discover the story of Nano Nagle and explore the historic buildings,
  gardens, and museum of Nano Nagle Place through a self-guided tour.
- **Highlights from the Presentation Sisters Congregational Archives** —
  Saturday 15th August | 12.00pm-4.00pm | Tea Room. A unique opportunity to
  explore a selection of historical artefacts from the Collections that shine
  a light on the fascinating history of Nano Nagle and the Presentation
  Sisters.
- **Researching the South Parish in Irish Census Records** — Saturday 15th
  August | 3.00pm | Global Hub. Learn how census records can unlock local and
  family histories, with practical insights into researching the South Parish
  through historical records.
- **\*CANCELLED\* — How to Look at Art: Summer School (2-Day Programme)** —
  Tuesday 18th & Wednesday 19th August | 10.30am-2.00pm | Conference Space.
- **Meet Nano Nagle with Judie Chalmers** — Wednesday 19th August | 1.00pm |
  Nano's Parlour. Actress Judie Chalmers brings the remarkable story of Nano
  Nagle in her parlour.
- **Foclóir Collage: Exploring Irish Through Art** — Thursday 20th August |
  1.00pm | Global Hub. Create your own artistic foclóir collage in this
  relaxed bilingual workshop celebrating Irish language and heritage.
  Suitable for all levels of Gaeilge.
- **A Genealogical Treasure Trove: Digitising the Registers of South Pres
  Primary School** — Saturday 22nd August | 11.30am-1.00pm | Global Hub.
  Speakers: Dr Danielle O'Donovan & Brendan Dempsey.

Alongside Heritage Week events, visitors can explore the award-winning Nano
Nagle Place Museum, heritage gardens, and historic buildings in the heart of
Cork city. Some events require advance booking.

Established in 1830, St Joseph's Cemetery is a historic graveyard located at Tory Top Road.
Originally known as Lilliput, it began as a Botanic Gardens from 1809 to 1828.

events.sourceName: Cork Heritage Open Day — historical walking tours
events.title: Capwell 100 Walking Tour with Cllr. Dan Boyle
events.raw:
In 1926 tenders were requested, part funded by reparation payments made by the British government as
compensation for the Burning of Cork, for the first major social housing in Cork City after the
establishment of the Irish Free State. This walk with Cllr. Dan Boyle explains how this came about and
its importance in Cork's development of the city. Meet at High Street/ Capwell Road Junction at 3pm.
Booking essential.
events.summary: Cllr Dan Boyle on the centenary of Capwell, Cork's first major Free State social housing, part-funded by British reparations for the Burning of Cork. Booking essential.

This time the Minions stumble into a mysterious world of creatures and monsters that pushes their chaotic curiosity to the absolute limit. Packed with the franchise’s trademark slapstick comedy, colourful animation and relentless visual gags, Minions & Monsters expands the universe with new characters, new villains and even bigger set-pieces. Since their introduction the Minions have become a true global phenomenon — spawning theme-park attractions, viral memes and billions of views online — thanks to their lovable stupidity and unstoppable enthusiasm for mayhem. With its combination of fast-paced comedy and family-friendly adventure, Minions & Monsters promises another wildly entertaining chapter for the most unpredictable characters in modern animation.

events.title: Super Troopers 3
events.raw:
**Super Troopers 3** (15A) — Mon 17 Aug 2026. Comedy. 1hr 44min.

Today's showtimes: 17:15 (Screen 9).

Super Troopers 3 sees the return of the most incompetent highway patrol officers in America, continuing a comedy franchise that has become one of the most unlikely cult success stories in modern cinema. The original Super Troopers arrived in 2001, created by comedy troupe Broken Lizard-Jay Chandrasekhar, Kevin Heffernan, Steve Lemme, Erik Stolhanske and Paul Soter-and quickly built a devoted following thanks to its absurd humour, endlessly quotable dialogue and ridiculous police antics. Although it was only a modest box-office performer on release, the film exploded in popularity through DVD and late-night screenings, eventually becoming a bona fide cult classic. That fan loyalty was proven spectacularly in 2015, when Broken Lizard launched a crowdfunding campaign to make Super Troopers 2-raising over $4.5 million in just 24 hours, at the time one of the fastest-funded movie campaigns ever. Now the moustached lawmen are back once again, with Jay Chandrasekhar returning to direct and the entire Broken Lizard team reprising their roles as the hilariously unprofessional Vermont State Troopers. Over the years the franchise has endured because of its unique blend of outrageous pranks, ridiculous authority figures and the chemistry between the comedy troupe themselves, who have continued making films together for more than two decades. With fans still quoting lines from the original film more than twenty years later, Super Troopers 3 promises more highway chaos, more ridiculous investigations and plenty of the absurd humour that has kept this unlikely comedy franchise alive for a generation.

events.description:
Rebel Comedy Club: Open Mic Night hosted by Graham Francis

Upstairs in the Franciscan Well. Doors @ 8:30pm. Starts 9pm!

Join us for a night of laughter at the Rebel Comedy Club's Open Mic
Night with hilarious performances from veteran comedians and some new
faces from Cork and beyond.

Whether you're a comedy enthusiast or just looking for a fun night out,
this night promises a great atmosphere with laughter throughout. You'd
be amazed at just how much wit, talent and humour we have right here in
Cork. Not to mention the acts who come from up the country and overseas
to showcase their stuff at our Open Mic and get a taste of what's
happening in Cork comedy.

Something special started happening in the Cork comedy scene in 2023.
Dozens of talented comedians have sprung up out of the open mics.
Established performers from around the country and abroad have started
visiting Cork far more frequently to perform. Some have even relocated
here. There are so many new clubs opening, with shows happening almost
everyday, often multiple gigs a night. The quality of comedy throughout
the county is rising rapidly. This explosion shows no signs of
stopping. So, come see these folks now before they're too famous!

Our Open Mic Night is the perfect platform for established veterans to
explore their new ideas and for aspiring comedians to practice material
and meet the pros. Expect a wide range of comedy styles and
personalities, with something for everyone to enjoy.

So gather your friends, grab a drink (and maybe a pizza from
downstairs), and get ready to laugh yourself silly at Rebel Comedy
Club's Open Mic Night. Don't miss out on this unique and historic time
in Cork Comedy!

events.description:
In 2026 we are delighted to be in a position to conserve and repair a number of
hugely important and significant collection pieces held at Fota House, which
are original to the property and connected to the Smith Barry estates including
10 early 19th century crested and carved walnut hall chairs, an 18th century
Irish giltwood and gesso table, a pair of bronze early 19th century candelabra,
two gesso and giltwood pier tables and a pair of decorative gilt wall sconces.

These conservation interventions will protect these items for the future and
ensure that they can be safely displayed for our visitors to enjoy.

To book your space, please email info@fotahouse.com

events.raw:
**The Past from the Press Exhibition** — June - September 2026.

We are delighted to host The Past from the Press, an exhibition on loan from
the National Library of Ireland. The Past from the Press will be on display at
Nano Nagle Place until September 2026.
events.summary: A National Library of Ireland touring show that treats newspapers as evidence you have to argue with - news values, bias, propaganda - and asks you to read between the lines of historic and current front pages alike.
events.description:
We are delighted to host **The Past from the Press**, an exhibition on loan
from the National Library of Ireland.

Newspapers are rich sources of information, offering valuable primary evidence
about the past. However, as with all historical material, there is more than
meets the eye. This thought-provoking exhibition explores themes such as news
values, bias, subjectivity, and propaganda, encouraging visitors to look more
closely and 'read between the lines' of both historic and contemporary
newspapers.

The Past from the Press will be on display at Nano Nagle Place until
September 2026.

We warmly invite you to visit, reflect, and discover how the stories of the
past continue to shape our understanding today.

Exhibition courtesy of the National Library of Ireland.

events.description:
Step into Cork's past at "Walls that Shaped a City", an engaging talk by Cork City Archaeologist, Ciara Brett, exploring the hidden story of the city's medieval defences. Once encircled by formidable stone walls, Cork was a walled settlement whose gates, towers, and fortifications shaped everyday life, trade, and security. Today, much of this legacy lies buried beneath streets and buildings – yet its impact endures.

Find out how archaeological digs have revealed fragments of walls, defensive ditches, and gateways that once defined the city's boundaries. Whether you are a history enthusiast, a local resident, or simply curious about the layers beneath your feet, "Walls that Shaped a City" offers a unique opportunity to connect with Cork's medieval origins and appreciate the foundations upon which the modern city stands.

events.description:
From the legends behind the Improv Panto, The Improv Murder Mystery and Getaway Outta That comes a brand-new theatrical riot Craic! The Improv Irish Play.

This is every classic Irish play you've ever seen and yet nothing you have ever witnessed before!

We're taking the sharp tongues of the tenements and the high-stakes feuds of the rural West and setting them on fire. Each night, the audience hand-pick the players from an arsenal of Irish stereotypes you've all seen before. From the pining Widow to the sharp-tongued Barkeep, the begrudging Priest to the mysterious Stranger, you decide who faces the music. Will there be blood-feud over a boundary ditch, a secret pregnancy, or a civil war in the snug!?

Featuring all your favourite improvisers: Laura O Mahony, Dominic MacHale, Laura Harte, John McCarthy and Declan Wolfe, with musician Dylan Howe conjuring haunting pipes and foot-stomping jigs on the fly.

Expect craic, razor-sharp wit, wild Irish dancing, and a total lack of restraint. No script. No safety net. Prepare for Cork Arts Theatre's most riotous, and unhinged summer highlights of the season!

events.title: Heritage Week: Butter in the Bog and A Pig in The Kitchen
events.raw:
**Heritage Week: Butter in the Bog and A Pig in The Kitchen, Tuesday 18th
August** — Tuesday 18th August 14.00- 15.30, The Firkin Crane. No Booking
Required.
events.summary: Make butter and brown bread by hand and plant a windowsill sprout garden, hung on 4,300 years of burying butter in bogs and keeping a pig on the buttermilk - the museum's Heritage Week argument about food security.
events.description:
Tuesday 18th August 14.00- 15.30, The Firkin Crane. No Booking Required.

We've buried butter in bogs in Ireland for at least 4300 years. Deep in the
bog, the butter stayed cool, safe, and secure: a way of taking a summer
surplus and preserving it for winter, when food was scarcer. We also kept
pigs who ate garden scraps, potato peels, and buttermilk from the butter
making process. Those pigs contributed fertiliser for the kitchen garden and
potato drills, and became another important food source in turn. Even the
brown bread on the table was part of the same thrifty logic, traditionally
made with wholegrain flour and fresh buttermilk (before the pigs got their
share!) These ingredients barely travelled further than the farmyard: food
miles you could probably count on one hand.

As climate change and geopolitical instability put questions of food security
back on the agenda, what can the past teach us about feeding ourselves well,
now and in the future? Can we re-discover food sources closer to home,
without relying on lorries, shipping lanes, or a supply chain with a thousand
points where something could go wrong? Join us to make butter and brown bread
by hand and plant seeds to sprout into delicious and nutritious "windowsill
gardens": a small piece of food security you can grow for yourself, even in
the city centre.

Sprouts Handout (A4) available to download.

events.description:
**Tuesday 18th – Saturday 22nd August at 8.00pm**

**Craic! The Improv Irish Play**

From the legends behind the **Improv Panto, The Improv Murder Mystery** and **Getaway Outta That** comes a brand-new theatrical riot, **Craic! The Improv Irish Play.**

This is every classic Irish play you’ve ever seen and yet nothing you have ever witnessed before!

We’re taking the sharp tongues of the tenements and the high-stakes feuds of the rural West and setting them on fire. Each night, the audience hand-pick the players from an arsenal of Irish stereotypes you’ve all seen before. From the pining Widow to the sharp-tongued Barkeep, the begrudging Priest, to the mysterious Stranger, you decide who faces the music. Will there be a blood-feud over a boundary ditch, a secret pregnancy, or a civil war in the snug!?

Featuring all your favourite improvisers: **Laura O Mahony, Dominic MacHale, Laura Harte, John McCarthy** and **Declan Wolfe,** with musician **Dylan Howe** conjuring haunting pipes and foot-stomping jigs on the fly.

Expect craic, razor-sharp wit, wild Irish dancing, and a total lack of restraint. No script. No safety net. Prepare for Cork Arts Theatre’s most riotous, and unhinged summer highlight of the season!

**CAST & CREATIVE TEAM:**

**Laura Harte**

**Laura O Mahony**

**Dominic MacHale**

**John McCarthy**

**Declan Wolfe**

events.title: Sustainable Toys – Making Dúchas Dolls!
events.raw:
**Sustainable Toys - Making Dúchas Dolls! Wednesday 19th August** —
WEDNESDAY 19th AUGUST, THE FIRKIN CRANE, 14.00 - 15.30 - NO BOOKING REQUIRED.
events.summary: Read what 1930s schoolchildren said about the dolls they made from yarn, pegs, straw and potatoes in the Dúchas folklore collection, then make two of them - a yarn doll and a peg doll.
events.description:
WEDNESDAY 19th AUGUST, THE FIRKIN CRANE, 14.00 - 15.30 - NO BOOKING REQUIRED

Long before the days of disposable blind boxes, screens, and planned
obsolescence, children across Ireland made their own toys. We know because
they told us so, and we also know exactly how they did it. The Dúchas
Schools' Collection of folklore, gathered in the late 1930s, is full of
first-hand accounts from children describing the dolls they made from
whatever was to hand: scraps of yarn, clothes pegs, straw, rags, potatoes,
sticks, and other found and leftover materials, along with a hefty helping of
imagination and ingenuity. In this workshop, we'll read some of these
accounts together, then recreate two of the dolls described in them (a yarn
doll and a peg doll).

Creativity and play build resilience, at any age. Join us to experience how
these old traditions of making, passed down hand-to-hand for hundreds of
years, can still teach us about the importance of creating our own fun: joy
without a price tag.

Dúchas Dolls Handout (A4) available to download.

events.description:
Outdoor theatre returns as Oddsocks Productions present their new adaptation of
Romeo and Juliet at Fota House as part of their UK & Ireland tour.

Finding both humour and heartfelt moments within one of Shakespeare's greatest
tragedies, this fresh interpretation brings new life to the story of two star
crossed lovers whose families are divided by an age old feud.

As the evening draws in, the grounds of Fota House become the setting for an
open air performance where theatre, history and the landscape come together
beneath the summer sky.

Bring a picnic, a blanket or chair, settle into the surroundings, and enjoy a
different way to experience theatre at Fota House.

events.title: Room Innate | Danny Foley
events.raw:
**Room Innate | Danny Foley** — 21 August – 25 September 2026, Studio
12. Tuesday – Friday 10 am – 5pm.
events.summary: Danny Foley's Moving Image Bursary show in Studio 12: black-and-white paintings, stop-motion, re-cut childhood footage and small clay figures, circling the Minotaur myth and the parts of a self you would rather not meet.
events.description:
*Room Innate* presents a new body of work by artist Danny Foley,
developed through the Backwater Artists Group Moving Image Bursary,
awarded to Foley in 2025. This installation explores artistic play as
a creative strategy for negotiating the self as shapeshifting,
multifaceted, and inherently vulnerable.

The exhibition encompasses black-and-white paintings on canvas, a
stop-motion video, re-edited archival footage from his childhood, and
small-scale clay sculptures that engage with uncertainty, doubt and
ambiguity.

Drawing on Jungian psychology, the work examines repressed aspects of
identity, referencing the myth of Theseus and the Minotaur. Rather
than presenting flawed aspects as something to eliminate, Foley
suggests these elements require "a different kind of encounter",
embracing contradiction and incompleteness.

events.summary: Half of Foghorn Stringband, touring their duo album Gold In Your Pocket — classic country, bluegrass and Cajun rather than the usual sorrowful trad.
events.description:
One half of world renowned Foghorn Stringband, Caleb & Reeb bring their
new duo album Gold In Your Pocket to the venue for 1 glorious night.

For Caleb Klauder & Reeb Willms, country music is soul music. Just as
soul music resonates the mind, body, and spirit with powerful rhythms
and expressive vocals, so too does the reflective storytelling and
crooning country music on their latest record, Gold In Your Pocket.
Blending classic country, bluegrass, old-time, and Cajun influences,
Caleb & Reeb offer a refreshing departure from the often sorrowful
themes found in traditional music. In fact, love — particularly
remembering, giving, and receiving it — is the thematic glue connecting
all 13 tracks. Celebrated for their charismatic performances and
deeply-rooted musical style, the duo's pared-down approach is
supplemented by pedal steel and electric guitar, channeling classic
country duos of old. Legendary Cajun musician and engineer Joel Savoy,
along with Nashville session savant Chris Scruggs, added tasteful
performances to Gold In Your Pocket.

events.title: Caroline Meaden and William McBride Immacolata
events.raw:
**Caroline Meaden and William McBride — Immacolata** — Residency 17/08/2026 – 21/08/2026, Smurfit Studio. **Showing Friday 21 August, 6pm.** FREE, booking encouraged.

Immacolata is a hypnotic dance work that draws audiences into an intimate, perceptual 'vortex'.
events.summary: The public showing at the end of a week's residency by the Melbourne dance artists, from a work built around clothing, drawing and dreamscape.
events.description:
Immacolata is a hypnotic dance work that draws audiences into an intimate, perceptual 'vortex'

Residency Showing Friday 21 August, 6pm

For information on Caroline's Professional Class on 20 August, click here.

The clothes of my partner and I steadily pile up onto a chair in the corner of my room. Half-worn, semi-structured and rumpled, they obscure any semblance of formal clarity. I sit and look at it, and impulsively draw shapes - crossing over one another, around again, looping back, no end point, no rest for the pencil. I painstakingly colour in all the little misshapen teardrops, circles and triangles that I can identify, dropping in water to wash the colour around. Thus delineated, they assemble into grotesque and ungainly tumors - born out of the chair itself.

Immacolata is a hypnotic dance work that draws audiences into an intimate, perceptual ‘vortex’, gathering quiet intensity through a refined movement language, unfolding within a scenographic frame. Emerging from a period of personal upheaval, the work has moved beyond autobiography to engage the body as a complex psychological and performative site. Rather than dictating meaning, Immacolata invites audiences into reflective encounters -.with purgatory, haunting and dreamscape.

" Immacolata has a beautiful sense of interiority, shaped by light, objects, and movement. It felt like a field of forces pulling me in—like a spool of thread, tightening and unravelling all at once. The work holds a compelling tension between precision and openness, with a clarity of movement and memory that lingers. ” - Amaara Raheem.

“ None of what I am experiencing is logical and I am attracted to that.” - Phillip Adams

Caroline Meaden and William McBride are Melbourne-based dance and performance artists working across choreography, performance, dramaturgy, and curatorial practice. They have collaborated for over a decade as co-directors of Alice Will Caroline (with Alice Dixon), and as choreographers and performers, sustaining individual and collaborative practices. Caroline is a dance artist and speech pathologist; William is an Alexander Technique teacher and Director of Temperance Hall, an experimental performance space where he provides dramaturgical guidance and developmental support for artists in residence.

Their work investigates the formal intelligence of dance as a time-based, relational artform. They approach choreography as a process of constructing and undoing rules: building systems that frame movement while allowing unconscious transmission, dissonance, and instability to surface. Rather than foregrounding overt thematic content, they derive structure from the dancing itself, attending to rhythm, proportion, fatigue, repetition, and breakdown.

Their work has been presented in festivals including Dance Massive, Next Wave, MEL&NYC Festival, Festival of Live Art, Melbourne Fringe and the Keir Choreographic Award. They have also been nominated for multiple awards, winning a Green Room Award for their work, Doors Shut, and three Melbourne Fringe Awards. With Alice Will Caroline, they were 2024 Co-Directors in Residence at Lucy Guerin Inc, and received a Chloe Munro Fellowship. Will and Caroline have collaborated and worked with notable artists including Phillip Adams Balletlab, Sandra Parker, Shelley Lasica, Monica Bill Barnes, Marina Abramovic, One Step at a Time Like This, Triage Live Art Collective, Walter Dundervill, Reckless Sleepers, Aphids and Opera Australia.

events.description:
**105 mins - United States 1990**

**Director:** Tim Burton

**Starring:** Johnny Depp, Winona Ryder and Dianne Wiest

High above the town in a lonely, gothic mansion, lived a man called Edward Scissorhands. His hands were cold but his heart was warm. You see Edward Scissorhands was not a real man - he is a creation. And his life forever changed the town where he lived. EDWARD SCISSORHANDS is a delightfully humorous, romantic and haunting fantasy that was a popular hit with critics and audiences back in the day. It is notable that this charming film features Vincent Price's last role released in his lifetime.

**The Fantastical Cinema of Tim Burton**

Tim Burton is a filmmaker with a unique cinematic vision in that his films often blend elements of gothic fantasy with whimsy and surrealism. Triskel Arts Centre is delighted to present Burton's first five feature films, which will be screened over five consecutive Saturday evenings this August.

> A fantasy that's cleverly original and both funny and bittersweet. — United Press International

events.description:
A City of Tails at Marina Market

22–28 August

Marina Market is delighted to be part of A City of Tails, a unique public
art trail in support of Irish Guide Dogs for the Blind.

Throughout the week, visitors to Marina Market can discover a selection of
beautifully decorated life-size dog sculptures, each uniquely designed by
local schools, artists, community groups, and businesses. Every sculpture
tells its own story while celebrating creativity, community, and the
life-changing work of Irish Guide Dogs.

The sculptures form part of a city-wide interactive art trail, with 50
striking dog sculptures displayed at locations across Cork from 22–28
August. Whether you're following the full trail or simply stopping by
Marina Market, it's the perfect opportunity to admire local artwork, take
some memorable photos, and support an incredible cause.

Come along, explore the sculptures, enjoy everything Marina Market has to
offer, and be part of this paws-itively inspiring event!

events.title: Haunted Spike
events.ageRestriction: Over 16's only, not suitable for younger children
events.raw:
**Haunted Spike** — Back by popular demand, hear personal tales and local
folklore of the hauntings of Spike Island. 22 August.
events.summary: Guides tell the island's own ghost stories - passed down by former residents and staff - in the unlit cells, punishment block and tunnels. No actors and no jump scares; the darkness does the work. Over 16s.
events.description:
Back by popular demand, hear personal tales and local folklore of the
**hauntings** of Spike Island. Join us on Saturday August 22nd, where we will see
if we can **make contact with the other side**.

> "A genuinely atmospheric, unsettling location"

Walking through creepy abandoned cells, punishment block, and dark underground
tunnels is a level of immersion that cannot be faked. Be ready for the
low-lighting and sometimes pitch darkness of these centuries old areas of our
fortress.

In the 19th century, Spike Island was one of the largest convict prisons in the
world, often called "Ireland's Hell," with overcrowding and harsh conditions
leading to many deaths. From this era of solitary confinement and children's
prisons, to Spike's use as a modern prison up until 2004, you're not just
hearing old folklore from our guides - you're getting stories spanning
centuries.

Our guides will recount the **paranormal stories and sightings**, passed down by
our former island residents and staff.

There are **no actors or jump scares.** Any fear you feel on the night comes from
atmosphere, darkness, and what you imagine - which for most people is far more
unsettling. You'll feel cut off from the world on our island which can only be
accessed by taking our ferry across Cork harbour.

Over 16's only, not suitable for younger children.

events.description:
THE GUILTEENS are a 4-piece from Cork City who have been quietly making
a name for themselves on the Irish and European music scene since
coming together in 2023. The band's sound is a mix of alternative, goth
and psych rock utilizing elements of blues and jazz instrumentation to
create a varied angular sound. 2025 saw the release of their debut
single 'Further Down The Channel' which caught the ears of French
independent record label LVP Records who released their debut EP
'Heavy Letters' and second single 'Born Evil' in November of last year.
The band have recently finished work on their debut album recorded by
Christian Best (Mick Flannery / Pôt-Pot) and mixed by John Spud Murphy
(Lankum, Black Midi, ØXN) due for release winter 2026.

SIR MARMALADE are a Dublin-based psych/garage band built on driving
kraut rhythms, fuzz-drenched riffs and hypnotic grooves that feel both
immediate and out of time. Their latest release Caligula / Tail-End
(Fuzzed Up & Astromoon Records) marks a clear step forward, with a
debut album currently in production. Known for self-produced shows
blending music, visuals and atmosphere, the band are building momentum
in Ireland while pushing toward UK and European audiences.

**BLACKPOOL BLOCK PARTY** — SUNDAY 23rd AUGUST 2026, Great William
O'Brien Street, in Blackpool, Cork. Free.

Free lunch and afternoon tea, live music, dancing, arts, games,

events.summary: Great William O'Brien Street closes to traffic for the day: three bands, a céilí, a repair café, street games and a free lunch cooked from community-garden produce. Free, and Cork City Council's Open Streets programme is behind the road closure.
events.description:
The Blackpool Block Party celebrates community and local culture on
Great William O'Brien Street. The event features live musical
performances, including Two Time Polka, Arundó and The Heppsters Jazz
Trio, plus workshops covering flash fiction, acrobatics, bike repair
and sustainable fashion.

Activities include knitting classes, a repair café, street games, art
installations and a céilí. Tiger Balm Supper Club provides
complimentary lunch featuring ingredients from community gardens,
followed by an afternoon tea party under a marquee.

The gardeners from Health Action Zone and Blackpool Men's Shed
distribute seasonal produce, planters, compost and seeds. The event is
organised by Cork Community Art Link and supported by multiple
community partners, operating as part of Cork City Council's Open
Streets programme to reclaim roadways as shared spaces for health and
wellbeing.

events.title: Blackpool Block Party
events.raw:
"NEXT BLOCK PARTY : SUNDAY 23rd AUGUST 2026"

"The Blackpool Block Party takes place on Sunday 23rd August on Great
William O'Brien Street, and as part of this years festivities we're
hosting a free lunch and afternoon tea for everyone, as well as live
music, dancing on the streets, arts, games, storytelling and plenty of
giveaways"
events.summary: A street closed for the day in Blackpool with five bands on stage, a free lunch cooked from Cork community-garden produce, an afternoon tea baked by residents, and workshops running all afternoon — acrobatics, bike and clothes repair, knitting, flash fiction and a céilí on the road.
events.description:
"The Blackpool Block Party takes place on Sunday 23rd August on Great
William O'Brien Street, in Blackpool, Cork, and is a celebration of
community and everything local. On stage we have Two Time Polka,
Arundó, The Heppsters Jazz Trio, French folk indie singer, Delta
Plane, and the Spangle Hill Band, as well as a diverse programme of
events throughout the afternoon."

"There will be flash fiction workshops with Graffiti Theatre, an art
installation called 'Hope Has Wings' produced by Cork City
Partnership, acrobatics workshop by Streetacro extraordinaire Ally
Futto, DIY bike repair workshops with Cork Community Bikes, DIY
clothes repair workshops and sustainable fashion related events with
Cork Environmental Forum and Restyle Ireland, gardening displays from
Meitheal Follaine and NICHE Community Gardens, smoothie bikes for a
healthy shake, a repair café where you can learn to fix your broken
stuff, knitting classes run by the Blackpool Knitting Group, a
Creative Garden display by Corlann Blackpool, a céilí on the street,
street games, craft stalls, clothes swaps, and plenty of books and
bric a brac to be given away."

"And that's not all, we'll be serving a free lunch (yes, there is such
a thing) cooked by the wonderful Tiger Balm Supper Club, with all the
ingredients coming from the many fantastic community gardens across
Cork City. Expect delicious salads, freshly baked breads, homemade
pickles and sauces followed by an afternoon tea party under our large
marquee, baked by the residents of Blackpool for the whole community
to enjoy."

"Best of all, the wonderful gardeners from the Health Action Zone and
the Blackpool Men's Shed, will be giving away the best seasonal
produce from our local community gardens, as well as free planters,
pots, compost and seeds, so you can grow your own at home."

"The Blackpool Block Party is produced by Cork Community Art Link and
kindly supported by SICAP, Cork City Council, Slaintecare, Safefood,
Health Action Zone, HSE, Blackpool Community Centre, Cork
Environmental Forum, Blackpool Credit Union, Cork Volunteer Centre and
local businesses. The event is also part of the Cork City Council Open
Streets programme."

"Experiment with different properties of water and discover how it

"Celebrate our rich heritage and explore this iconic landmark of the
city's skyline. Discover Cork City's challenge and solution to provide

wetlands. Water Heritage Day celebrates water throughout Ireland, its
history and heritage and our connections with it."

events.description:
NEXT BLOCK PARTY : SUNDAY 23rd AUGUST 2026

The Blackpool Block Party takes place on Sunday 23rd August on Great
William O'Brien Street, in Blackpool, Cork, and is a celebration of
community and everything local. On stage we have Two Time Polka,
Arundó, The Heppsters Jazz Trio, French folk indie singer, Delta Plane,
and the Spangle Hill Band, as well as a diverse programme of events
throughout the afternoon.

There will be flash fiction workshops with Graffiti Theatre, an art
installation called 'Hope Has Wings' produced by Cork City Partnership,
acrobatics workshop by Streetacro extraordinaire Ally Futto, DIY bike
repair workshops with Cork Community Bikes, DIY clothes repair
workshops and sustainable fashion related events with Cork
Environmental Forum and Restyle Ireland, gardening displays from
Meitheal Follaine and NICHE Community Gardens, smoothie bikes for a
healthy shake, a repair café where you can learn to fix your broken
stuff, knitting classes run by the Blackpool Knitting Group, a Creative
Garden display by Corlann Blackpool, a céilí on the street, street
games, craft stalls, clothes swaps, and plenty of books and bric a brac
to be given away.

And that's not all, we'll be serving a free lunch (yes, there is such a
thing) cooked by the wonderful Tiger Balm Supper Club, with all the
ingredients coming from the many fantastic community gardens across
Cork City. Expect delicious salads, freshly baked breads, homemade
pickles and sauces followed by an afternoon tea party under our large
marquee, baked by the residents of Blackpool for the whole community to
enjoy.

Best of all, the wonderful gardeners from the Health Action Zone and
the Blackpool Men's Shed, will be giving away the best seasonal produce
from our local community gardens, as well as free planters, pots,
compost and seeds, so you can grow your own at home.

The Blackpool Block Party is produced by Cork Community Art Link and
kindly supported by SICAP, Cork City Council, Slaintecare, Safefood,
Health Action Zone, HSE, Blackpool Community Centre, Cork Environmental
Forum, Blackpool Credit Union, Cork Volunteer Centre and local
businesses. The event is also part of the Cork City Council Open
Streets programme.

events.description:
Experience beekeeping in a traditional Irish cottage garden, where our native
Irish honey bees play a vital part in the homestead ecosystem. Surrounded by
flowers, herbs, fruit and seasonal kitchen garden produce, this hands-on
experience takes guests through the pollinator-rich garden and into the apiary
to observe how bees make honey, from flower to jar.

Suit up and step inside a working apiary with beekeeper Hanna Bäckmo, open a
beehive and get a close-up look at a living honey bee colony. The experience
also includes a guided tasting of seasonal Irish honeys, refreshments and
plenty of time to ask questions about bees, beekeeping and the important
relationship between pollinators, gardens and our food.

Gain an insight into a slower, more connected way of living while learning
about bees, pollination and honey production as part of everyday life in a
working cottage garden.

Advance booking is essential. Places are limited.

arrangements and dynamic live energy to audiences across the country.

events.description:
Join conservator Karen Horton for a fascinating free talk exploring the
conservation and redisplay of some of Nano Nagle's most treasured relics and

conservation of a significant collection belonging to the Union of
Presentation Sisters. This engaging talk will delve into the redevelopment of

historical objects, and the importance of building trust with stakeholders
throughout the process.

Karen will also share the remarkable story of the conservation of one of the
collection's most important relics, Nano Nagle's Silk Apron, and discuss the
redisplay of these treasured artefacts for future generations.

📅 Tuesday, 25 August | 1pm

events.summary: Thaís Muniz discusses her film *The Kite Ballet* with researcher Dr Eve Olney, closing out Crawford's Artists Film International season at Triskel. Free and unticketed.
events.description:
Crawford Art Gallery and Triskel Arts Centre present "In Conversation:
Artist Thaís Muniz and Dr Eve Olney", part of Artists Film
International 2026 under the theme *A Kind of Power*. The discussion
centres on Muniz's film *The Kite Ballet*.

**About Thaís Muniz:** her practice investigates "intersections
between inherited and acquired identities, memory, transit, and
interior love". Her work spans photography, film, performance,
installation and sculpture, with an emphasis on community engagement
and collective learning. She holds an MA from IADT Dublin and has
exhibited internationally.

**About Dr Eve Olney:** a researcher and consultant specialising in
sustainable creative practices, Olney co-founded Cork Community Land
Trust and is a postdoctoral researcher at MTU's Department of
Architecture, working on radical pedagogies in design and architecture
education.

Moderated by curator Dawn Williams.

events.raw:
**The Rocket's Red Glare** — August 27 - October 3, 2026.
Sample-Studios Gallery: The Lord Mayor's Pavilion, Fitzgerald's Park.
Admission free.

Solo exhibition by Barbara Diener.
events.summary: Barbara Diener on Wernher von Braun — the Nazi engineer who became a NASA hero — folding in photographs her own grandfather took on the Eastern Front in 1941-42, with mixed-reality elements pushing against the documentary frame.
events.description:
This solo exhibition by Barbara Diener examines "the life and legacy
of German rocket scientist Wernher von Braun, exploring the selective
ways history is recorded and remembered". The work addresses von
Braun's dual role as a Nazi engineer and celebrated NASA scientist,
reflecting on how "innovations developed for warfare also enabled
space exploration" while certain historical aspects were obscured.

Diener incorporates her own family narrative, reprinting photographs
her grandfather took in 1941/42 while serving in the German Army. The
exhibition connects personal and broader historical themes through
photographs and archival material, examining memory, landscape and
environmental responsibility. Mixed Reality elements challenge
conventional documentary approaches, "creating new connections between
the physical world and constructed narratives".

events.description:
Thursday 27th – Saturday 29th August @ 8pm
plus Lunchtime shows: Friday and Saturday @ 1pm

**Úna Ní Bhriain and Jenny Whyte present**

**Sídh: Stories of Women from Irish Mythology**

**Sídh** is a new theatrical storytelling performance that weaves together a collection of stories of mythological Irish women navigating power, war, resilience, desire, love, loss, and transformation.

Performed by **Úna Ní Bhriain**, the work draws on her lifelong connection to traditional Irish storytelling as the daughter of a seanchaí. This piece marks a new step in her practice, bridging storytelling and contemporary performance.

Developed in collaboration with director **Jenny Whyte**, whose scenographic approach elevates and enriches the sensory and visual world of the piece, _Sídh_ blends the intimacy of the seanchaí tradition with theatrical design.

In this shared space between storyteller and audience, tales of ancient goddesses, warriors, queens, and otherworldly beings feel both timeless and strikingly present today.

Created & Performed by **Úna Ní Bhriain**

Created & Directed by **Jenny Whyte**

Producer / Production Manager: **Michael-Anthony Greene**

Photography: **Eoin McAulay**

**Running time:** 60mins – no interval

**Age recommendation:** 12+

events.summary: First of two sold-out nights of Pinotphile, the follow-up to Joanne McNally's record-breaking Prosecco Express.
events.description:
Record-breaking queen of Irish comedy Joanne McNally brings her new
tour 'Pinotphile' to Cork.

'Pinotphile' follows the runaway success of Joanne's smash hit 'The
Prosecco Express' – a show that set off on its maiden voyage in initial
previews back in 2019 before becoming a critically acclaimed global
riot – touring across UK, Ireland, Australia, Dubai, Canada and the US
– where media giant Variety tipped Joanne as one of its comedy 'Ones to
Watch'. Back home, Ticketmaster IE crowned the show its 'Comedy Event
of the Year' following an unprecedented 78 show run at Dublin's Vicar
Street.

Since then, McNally has been keeping herself busy by ruining men's
lives (and her own) – still single, still unfertilised, and laden with
irreverent, ridiculous and hilarious war stories, join Joanne for a
wild ride in 'Pinotphile', as she navigates situationships, revenge,
frenemies and rejection in her 'terrifyingly funny' (London Standard)
and 'joyously nuts' (Irish Examiner) trademark style.

One of podcasting's best loved names, Joanne is the co-host of the
award-winning 'My Therapist Ghosted Me' alongside best friend Vogue
Williams – since launching in 2021, the podcast reaches over 2.5
million listeners per month and has toured across the world,
culminating in an extraordinary run of 5 sold out nights at Dublin's 3
Arena.

Elsewhere, Joanne also hosts the hugely popular BBC Sounds format
Joanne McNally Investigates – with two series under her belt – 'Who
Replaced Avril Lavigne?' and 'Do Furbys Spy On Us?'. A primetime TV
regular, Joanne is best known for her riotous appearances on
Taskmaster, The Jonathan Ross Show, The Big Fat Quiz of Everything, and
many more.

SPECIAL EFFECTS: This production may contain Strobe Lighting, Flashing
Lights, Smoke and Haze.

AGE GUIDANCE: Under 16's must be accompanied by an adult

Tim Burton returned to the streets of Gotham City to make a sequel to his colossal box office hit BATMAN and the result is a film that many consider to be even better than the original. This installment of the Batman franchise sees the Dark Knight pitted against an array of diabolical villains - the vicious Penguin with his umbrellaful of evil tricks, the sensuous and mysterious feline temptress, Catwoman, and the scheming mega-millionaire Max Shreck.

**The Fantastical Cinema of Tim Burton**

events.description:
Singer/Songwriter Mick Hanly with fellow Moving Hearts members, Anto
Drennan and Eoghan O'Neill for a night of stories and songs.

Limerick born Singer/Songwriter Mick Hanly, now longtime resident of
Thomastown, Co. Kilkenny teams up with fellow Moving Hearts members,
Anto Drennan and Eoghan O'Neill for a gig in The White Horse Inn,
Ballincollig, Cork. The trio have done a string of gigs since the start
of the year to much acclaim. Hanly spent two years as a wages clerk in
the ESB in Galway, but his love of music was such that he quit his job
to pursue a musical career. Today, he is regarded as one of Ireland's
best songwriters, and his songs have been covered by luminaries such as
Mary Black, Christy Moore and Dolores Keane. His song Past The Point of
Rescue went to No. 2 in the American Country charts for singer Hal
Ketchum and has earned him the BMI award for 2 million radio plays in
the US. The guitar skills of Anto Drennan are widely sought after by
such luminaries as Mike & The Mechanics and The Corrs.

**94 mins - United Kingdom 1996**

**Director:** Danny Boyle

**Starring:** Ewan McGregor, Ewen Bremner and Jonny Lee Miller

Hilarious but harrowing, this film is the story of Mark Renton and his friends Sick Boy, Spud, Begbie and Tommy, and charts the disintegration of their friendship as they proceed, seemingly inevitably, towards self-destruction. Mark alone has the insight and opportunity to escape his fate - but then again, does he really want to "choose life"? Based on the novel by Irvine Welsh, TRAINSPOTTING is one of the seminal movies of the nineties. To mark its 30th anniversary, do not miss seeing this film back on the big screen.

**A Nation Once Again - Paul Howard in conversation with Mick Clifford** — Tuesday 1st September 2026,
18:30 – 20:00, Waterstones Cork. €19, General Admission €5.

Bestselling author Paul Howard in conversation with Mick Clifford.
events.summary: Paul Howard, creator of Ross O'Carroll-Kelly, reads from and discusses his United Ireland satire A Nation Once Again with journalist Mick Clifford. Ticketed.
events.description:
We are delighted to welcome Paul Howard to Waterstones Cork to read from and discuss his new novel A
Nation Once Again.

Paul is a journalist, author and comedy writer best known as the creator of the No 1 bestselling Ross
O'Carroll-Kelly series. He has won a record four Irish Book Awards and is a former Irish Sports
Journalist of the Year and Irish Newspaper Columnist of the Year.

In the hilarious *A Nation Once Again* we meet Fiach O'Bric: career diplomat, recent widower, and a man
looking forward to a peaceful retirement. But just when he thinks he's out, he is strong-armed into taking
over a shadowy top-secret department tasked with preparing for a United Ireland — a job so surreal it
makes his last posting, in Beijing, seem like a Buddhist retreat.

> I had a great time reading A Nation Once Again. It is hilarious, bang-on, even slightly disturbing -
> everything I love about Paul Howard's writing. — Roddy Doyle

> Funny, smart and provocative, the scariest thing about this novel is that it might be based on fact. —
> John Boyne

Paul will be joined for this event by Mick Clifford, one of Ireland's leading journalists and a writer
with a keen eye for the satirical and the absurd.

events.description:
**Thursday 3rd – Friday 4th September @ 8:00 pm**

**By the Light of the Silvery Moon**

Following sold-out performances and widespread acclaim, award-winning storyteller, musician and modern-day seanchaí Aindrias de Staic brings his celebrated live production, **By the Light of the Silvery Moon,** to Cork Arts Theatre as part of a national tour.

The show breathes vibrant new life into Ireland’s ancient storytelling tradition through an unforgettable fusion of folklore, live music and theatrical performance.

Inspired by the great Irish bards—including Raifteirí an File, Brian Merriman and Aindrias Mac Cruitín—Aindrias takes audiences on a journey through myth, memory and the rich oral traditions of the West of Ireland. With rustic fiddle in hand and his unmistakable storytelling style, he conjures a world of forgotten villages, wandering musicians, mischievous spirits and otherworldly encounters, delivered with warmth, humour and irresistible theatrical energy.

Joining Aindrias on stage are acclaimed musicians Brian Fleming (percussion) and Aisling Lyons (harp), whose richly textured live score transforms each story into an immersive experience. Together, they create a captivating interplay of rhythm, melody and spoken word, weaving a sonic landscape that carries audiences from moments of laughter to mystery and wonder.

Rooted in tradition yet unmistakably contemporary, By the Light of the Silvery Moon is more than a performance—it’s an invitation into Ireland’s living heritage, where ancient tales find a new voice for modern audiences. Rich in folklore, music, and imagination, this is an evening of spellbinding storytelling that lingers long after the final note.

**REVIEWS:**

_**“He breathes new life into the old tales – infusing them with musicality, rhythm and his unique insights on life”**_

– Manchán Magan

_**“Our culture needs spirits like this, a wayward Irish fiddle playing dream talker”**_

– Tommy Tiernan

**TEAM:**

**Aindrias de Staic** – storyteller/seanchaí

**Brian Fleming** – bodhrán

**The Rime Of The Ancient Mariner**

Directed by **Sue Hill**

Performed by **John O’Mahony**

A spellbinding theatrical retelling of Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s timeless masterpiece, The Rime of the Ancient Mariner. Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s story of an epic sea journey, written in 1797, centres around the killing of a harmless sea-bird – the albatross. The havoc wreaked by this pointless act of vandalism explodes into one of the most popular and best-loved poems in the English language – an epic tale of guilt, redemption, and humanity’s relationship with the natural world.

In an age that is increasingly aware of humanity’s relationship to, and dependence upon, the environment, Coleridge’s ‘poem of the biosphere’ is undergoing a popular revival. And no wonder; it is a rollicking good yarn suffused with elements of the gothic and the downright ghostly…

**REVIEW**

_“This Rime Of The Ancient Mariner is a thoroughly absorbing piece of theatre, flawlessly performed by an actor drawing upon a wide experience of theatre of all kinds.”_

events.title: RAPT By Benjamin Richter Company
events.raw:
**RAPT By Benjamin Richter Company** — 05/09/2026, 7:30 pm, Smurfit Theatre. €15/€12 concession.

Presented as part of UpDown Circus Festival.
events.summary: A contemporary juggling piece made with grass paper, presented as part of the UpDown Circus Festival.
events.description:
Presented as part of UpDown Circus Festival RAPT begins with our problematic relationship to the word “more” - a concept that has brought humanity both growth and self-destruction, leaving us teetering between ecstatic pleasure and absolute catastrophe. Through the tools of contemporary juggling, a tragicomic associative journey unfolds, in which human and paper, care and waste, transience and crumpled matter become entangled.

We understand circus as an instrument for illuminating themes of life from unusual, virtuosic, or surprising perspectives. Our contemporary juggling is strongly influenced by the philosophy of object-oriented ontology, which proposes that non-human objects possess their own agency - independent of humans. On stage, an object or prop becomes an equal playing partner, and a dialogue emerges. This dialogue can expand our understanding of things, beings, and objects, and call into question any assumption of human superiority.

In RAPT, we work with grass paper composed of 60% grass fibers and 40% recycled paper. Our aim is to produce as little paper waste as possible and to continually reuse the material - with all its traces of wear and in ever-changing forms. The production is designed to be as sustainable as possible, and in the end the entire piece fits into just two suitcases. Rather than leaving an ever-greater footprint, we choose to cultivate a hopeful handprint.

Benjamin Richter is a pioneering juggling artist working at the intersections of contemporary circus and dance for over 35 years. Influenced by new materialist philosophies and clowning, he has developed a unique choreographic style encompassing his playful object-oriented and improvisational practices.

He creates and performs in various collaborations and has worked with Gandini Juggling, Cirkus Cirkör, the Bauhaus Dessau Foundation and Atemzug. He has performed his own works in over 25 countries worldwide, including appearances at the Berliner Tanztage, LIMF, and the Edinburgh International Fringe Festival.

From his beginnings as a street performer, Benjamin has spent decades in artistic research, sharing insights though creating, teaching, deconstructing and enriching both his own practices and those of countless other artists. He has designed courses and taught BA, MA, PHD and independent students at the Stockholm University of the Arts since 2003, where he designed and led the Artistic Development Course. Benjamin currently holds a professorship at the École Superieur des Arts du Cirque in Brussels. **Book launch: Setting the Land Free by Eoghan Daltun** — Wednesday 9th September 2026, 18:30 – 20:00,
Waterstones Cork.

Join us for the launch of Setting the Land Free by Eoghan Daltun in which the author of An Irish Atlantic
Rainforest travels across Ireland and beyond to Scotland and Costa Rica meeting pioneers in restoration
and regeneration.
events.summary: Beara rewilder Eoghan Daltun launches Setting the Land Free, following his An Post award-winning An Irish Atlantic Rainforest.
events.description:
Join us for the launch of *Setting the Land Free* by Eoghan Daltun.

Eoghan Daltun is a sculpture conservator, a farmer, an author and, above all, a rewilder. Reared in
Dublin, he has travelled widely, as well as living abroad in London, Paris and Prague. He spent seven
years studying sculpture in Carrara, Tuscany. In 2009, he sold the cottage in Kilmainham he had rebuilt
mostly single-handed from a ruin — dating back to at least the 1750s — using the original stone. The
proceeds went to buy a long-abandoned 73-acre farm overlooking the Atlantic near Eyeries on the Beara
Peninsula, West Cork. Much of the land was covered in wild native forest which, although very beautiful,
was ecologically wrecked by severe overgrazing and invasion by a host of alien plant species. Over the
years since, Eoghan has brought life in all its explosive vibrancy back to the land, with new temperate
rainforest spontaneously forming where previously there was only barren grass. Restoring such an
incredibly rich ecosystem has taken him on a fantastic voyage of discovery, which he charted in his
memoir An Irish Atlantic Rainforest: A Personal Journey into the Magic of Rewilding, which won an An Post
Irish Book Award in 2022. Rewilding most of the land, and High Nature Value farming the rest, has given
him plenty of time to reflect deeply on the ecological crisis unfolding at terrifying speed all around
us, and its solutions. Eoghan followed this up in 2024 with a stunning full-colour illustrated book, The
Magic of an Irish Rainforest: A Visual Journey, in which he travelled the length and breadth of Ireland
photographing areas of temperate rainforest, in a bid to illustrate their beauty and immense ecological
value, and to document, in almost all cases, their state of decline.

In *Setting the Land Free*, Eoghan travels across Ireland and beyond to Scotland and Costa Rica,
encountering pioneers restoring bogs, reintroducing native species and regenerating forests and
coastlines.

events.description:
The UK's leading political comic is back on tour.

The world is in chaos. Inequality is widening, autocracy is rising and
political parties are collapsing. In these divided times, what this
country desperately needs is Angry Humour From a Really Nice Guy (in
many ways it's actually the last thing this country needs, but it's
what it's getting so tough luck).

The UK's leading political comic Nish Kumar – co-host of hugely popular
podcast Pod Save the UK, former host of axed BBC show The Mash Report,
and one of Taskmaster's greatest losers – is back on tour with a
formidable batch of passionate, progressive stand-up for the ages.

Kumar is 40. His mind is breaking. His body is worse. Expect
existential angst and political disquiet from comedy's cheekiest boy.
Nish Kumar was named one of the 50 Best Comedians of the 21st Century
by both The Guardian and The Telegraph, with his previous tour playing
to sold out crowds across the UK, North America, Australasia and
mainland Europe.

SPECIAL EFFECTS: This production may contain Strobe Lighting, Flashing

Clothes Cycle Cork

Saturday 12 September 2026 | 11am–6pm

Marina Market, Centre Park Road, Cork

Europe's biggest thrift festival is coming to Cork!

Get ready for a huge 25,000+ sq ft immersive thrifting experience
featuring 100+ curated sellers, vintage, Y2K, streetwear, designer and
luxury pieces, archive fashion, bargains, handmade items, jewellery, shoes

DJs, street food, coffee and bakes, a free clothes swap, free alterations,

**Clothes Swap**

Bring up to 5 pre-loved clothing items, shoes, bags or hats and exchange
them for tokens to shop the swap section.

- 11am–12pm: Drop-off only
- 12pm–5pm: Drop-off or pick-up
- 5pm–6pm: Leftover items are FREE

The first 150 attendees receive a free tote bag, with more freebies and
giveaways throughout the day.

Children 12 and under and carers go free.

Tickets may not be available on the door due to high demand.

No dogs allowed. All sellers accept cash and card.

events.description:
On Saturday 12th September, Clothes Cycle will take over the iconic Marina
Market, transforming it into a one-day thrifting festival. The event will bring
together more than 100 local vintage and preloved fashion sellers for a huge
day of shopping, music, food, and sustainable fashion.

Far more than a vintage market, Clothes Cycle has become one of the UK's
fastest-growing fashion events, creating a completely new way to experience
second-hand shopping. From archive designer pieces and curated vintage
collections to €2 bargain rails, visitors can expect something for every style
and every budget.

Whether you're a serious vintage collector, looking to refresh your wardrobe
sustainably, or simply after a great day out with friends, Clothes Cycle
promises an experience unlike any other currently on offer in Ireland.

Visitors can expect:

- A free, all-day clothes swap - bring up to five items and swap them for
  something new.
- DJs and live music throughout the day.
- Street food, a fully stocked bar, and plenty of chill-out areas and outdoor
  seating.
- A free alteration station.
- Pop-ups including permanent jewellery, tooth gems, and tattoos.
- Thousands of curated vintage pieces.
- Fun giveaways throughout the day, including free tote bags for the first 150
  attendees.

events.title: 5K RUN
events.timesText: Boats depart from Cobh at 4pm and 4:45pm; race kicks off at approximately 5:25 p.m.
events.raw:
**5K RUN** — 12 September 2026. Back by popular demand! We're delighted to
announce the return of our Spike Island 5km Race. Lace up your running shoes and
join us on Saturday 12th September for an unforgettable run on Ireland's
infamous prison island.
events.summary: A 5km starting inside the walls of a 200-year-old fortress and looping the island, chip-timed for the first time in 2026. Boats out of Cobh at 4pm and 4:45pm, gun at about 5:25pm, medal and a ceremony after.
events.description:
Back by popular demand! We're delighted to announce the return of our Spike
Island 5km Race. Lace up your running shoes and join us on Saturday 12th
September for an unforgettable run on Ireland's infamous prison island.

This unique event promises an adventure like no other – where else can you begin
your race within the walls of a 200-year-old fortress before making your way
around an iconic island surrounded by spectacular views of Cork Harbour?

New in 2026, we are using a chip timing system to give you the most accurate
timings possible, available online for you to see soon after the event has
finished.

The race kicks off at approximately 5:25 p.m., promising an adrenaline-fueled
dash through the island's scenic routes. Our dedicated marshals will be on hand
to guide you and ensure you stay on track throughout.

After crossing the finish line, each participant will receive a special Spike
Island medal and there will be a special medal ceremony to celebrate your
triumphs, with awards for the fastest male and female runners.

So what are you waiting for? Embrace the challenge and create lasting memories at
Spike Island. Boats depart from Cobh at 4pm and 4:45pm and spaces are limited for
this unique race event.

**Culture Night — Film Screening: Mná na DXP** — 18 September. Date: Friday, 18
September. Time: 5 - 7 pm. Venue: Mitchel Hall and C-Class Cells at Spike
Island. Tickets will be available soon.
events.summary: A fourteen-minute documentary on thirty years of the Dillon's Cross Project, which supports Cork women whose lives have been shaped by a family member's imprisonment - screened, pointedly, in a prison, with the women themselves speaking afterwards.
events.description:
**Culture Night at Spike Island** will feature a screening of **Mná na DXP**, a
powerful 14-minute documentary marking 30 years of the Dillon's Cross Project
(DXP), a Cork City education centre supporting women whose lives have been
affected by the incarceration of loved ones within the Irish prison system.

Through the women's own voices, Mná na DXP reflects on resilience, friendship and
the strong sense of belonging fostered through the Dillon's Cross Project over
the past three decades.

The documentary was directed by Cork-based printmaker and visual artist Paul La
Rocque. As a teacher with the Dillon's Cross Project, Paul brings a unique insight
and perspective to the film.

The event will begin with an introduction exploring the development of the
documentary and the collaborative process behind its creation, followed by a
short Q&A before the screening. After the film, women from the Dillon's Cross
Project will share their personal experiences, reflecting on the impact the
project has had on their lives, their families and their community.

Title: Mná na DXP. Director: Paul La Rocque. Editing and Music: Caoilian
Sherlock. Graphics: Aoife La Rocque. Duration: 14 minutes.

Date: Friday, 18 September. Time: 5 - 7 pm. Venue: Mitchel Hall and C-Class Cells
at Spike Island. Tickets will be available soon.
