events.title: I Fall Down: A Restoration Comedy Gina Moxley
events.raw:
**I Fall Down: A Restoration Comedy — Gina Moxley** — 18/09/2026 – 20/09/2026, Daily 7.30pm, Sunday Matinee 2pm. €20/€18.

I Fall Down is an immersive, punk and fearlessly feminist show by Gina Moxley.
events.summary: Gina Moxley's promenade show on the erasure of women from art history, moving between locations and ending in a clay-modelling workshop. A co-production with The Everyman and Once Off Productions.
events.description:
I Fall Down is an immersive, punk and fearlessly feminist show by Gina Moxley

” Fearlessly ambitious, both scrappily punk and technically proficient… I Fall Down is fun, funny and unapologetically feminist. “

— Business Post

” Outrageous comedy.“

— The Irish Times

In I Fall Down, Gina Moxley, a former art student, begins by referring to what was her introductory bible to art history - The Story of Art - in which not a single female artist was mentioned. Enraged by that erasure and inspired by Florence Syndrome, a malady where tourists are so overwhelmed by seeing classical masterpieces, they fall into a psychotic state, Moxley confronts classical female statuary head on. The omission of their genitalia propels her on a wild mission to set the record straight.

This immersive, punk and fearlessly feminist show begins with a lecture, segues into an operatic promenade, travels to Florence courtesy of contemporary dance, video and sound installations and finally arrives at a cheeky hands-on clay modelling workshop. A living example of Joseph Beuys' radical dictum: 'Everyone is an artist'. Possibly the best fun you can have getting your hands dirty.

A 'restoration comedy' so to speak.

I Fall Down is a critical and audience hit, appealing to audiences of all genders and across a huge age range from sixteen to ninety-six.

Originally staged across multiple spaces at the Crawford Art Gallery for the Cork Midsummer Festival and restaged at Trinity College Dublin for the Dublin Theatre Festival.

A Co-production between The Everyman and Once Off Productions. Funded by the Arts Council | An Chomhairle Ealaíon

Please note This is a promenade performance and will require moving by foot to different locations. For ages 16+

Gina Moxley is an award-winning writer, actor and director based in Dublin, Ireland. She has been involved in Irish theatre for the past forty years. A Fine Art graduate, she also holds an M.Phil in Creative Writing.

Her first play Danti-Dan was produced by Rough Magic in 1995 and won the Stewart Parker Award. Since then she has written for companies such as Pan Pan, CoisCéim, Fishamble, Cork Capital of Culture, Controvento and National Connections UK. Her play The Patient Gloria, which she also performs in, has had hugely successful runs at St Ann's Warehouse in New York and at Brighton Festival. Previously presented by the Abbey Theatre for Dublin Theatre Festival and at the Traverse Theatre, Edinburgh, where it won a Fringe First and Herald Angel. The show toured in Ireland in spring 2023. Her most recent piece, I FALL DOWN premiered at the Crawford Art Gallery in association with The Everyman Theatre for Cork Midsummer Festival 2023, and was restaged as part of Dublin Theatre Festival in 2025.

She has written several radio plays broadcast by RTE and has published some short stories.

Gina has toured extensively with companies such as Pan Pan,Dead Centre and Tim Crouch to festivals in Europe, Asia, USA, Australia and New Zealand. ​

She has been collaborating with artist, Sean Lynch, for over a decade, including his show Adventure:Capital which represented Ireland at the Venice Biennale 2015.

​

She was Irish Patron Playwright at New Plays from Europe Biennale, Wiesbaden, Germany from 2010 to 2014. In 2020, she was elected to Aosdána, an affiliation of Irish artists that have produced a distinguished body of work.

Writer Gina Moxley

Director John McIlduff

Original Choreography Emily Terndrup

Tour Choreography Katherine O'Malley

Performers Gina Moxley, Amy Ní Fearraigh, Bláithín Mac Gabhann, Katherine O'Malley, Anne Rowe

ABOUT ONCE OFF PRODUCTIONS

Founded in 2006 by Maura O’Keeffe, Once Off Productions provides a structured, supportive and creative producing platform for independent performance artists making ambitious, innovative and collaborative work. Working nationally and internationally at all scales, the company is committed to bringing live performance to audiences in traditional and non-traditional locations.

Once Off Productions facilitates artists to make work outside of traditional company structures while simultaneously offering all of the advantages of producing and administrative support. The Company enables some of the most brilliant and exciting artists based in Ireland to create, develop and present new work for a wide range of audiences.

Since 2020, the company has been funded through a new Arts Council ‘Creative Production Services’ initiative which has allowed the platform and team to expand to provide consolidated, resourced & expert supports to the independent performing arts sector as well as training, mentoring and employment opportunities for producers and production managers.

Once Off Productions is a key part of the performing arts landscape in Ireland, nurturing artists and fostering the development of innovative, collaborative, courageous and ambitious projects while marrying this work with the needs of presenters to serve audiences across the island of Ireland and internationally.

ABOUT THE EVERYMAN

The Everyman’s mission is to produce the best in Irish and international performance for Cork and Irish audiences. We aim to be indispensable to all of the communities we serve: audiences, artists, employees and suppliers, while remaining rooted in, and inextricably linked to, Cork.

We work hard to support and enrich the cultural fabric of our country by delivering an ambitious programme in a beautiful venue that serves the audience of today and builds the audience of the future.

Our Vision is to be an internationally recognised centre of excellence for theatre in Ireland and a vibrant cultural centre for Cork.

Funded by the Arts Council | An Chomhairle Ealaíon

events.title: Cork Echo Women's Mini Marathon 2026
events.raw: **45th Annual Echo Women's Mini-Marathon** — Centre Park Road, Cork. 1pm Sunday, September 20th 2026. Organised and hosted by Cork Athletics; course measured by John Quigley, AIMS/World Athletics Grade 'A' Measurer. 6km. [Enter 45th Echo Women's Mini-Marathon](https://eventmaster.ie/event/lMeysV8HPO) · [Echo Mini-Marathon website](https://theechominimarathon.ie/) · Wheelchair participants start at 12:45pm sharp.
events.summary: The 45th Echo Women's Mini Marathon, the biggest event of its kind in Munster, with over 10,000 taking part in recent years. A 6km run, jog or walk starting on Centre Park Road at 13:00 and finishing on Monahan Road beside Kennedy Park; wheelchair entrants go off at 12:45.
events.description:
45th Annual Echo Women's Mini-Marathon

Centre Park Road, Cork. 1pm Sunday, September 20th 2026.

This event is organised and hosted by Cork Athletics. This course was measured by John Quigley, AIMS/World Athletics Grade 'A' Measurer.

- [Enter 45th Echo Women's Mini-Marathon](https://eventmaster.ie/event/lMeysV8HPO)
- [Echo Mini-Marathon website](https://theechominimarathon.ie/)
- [Echo Mini-Marathon event Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/theechominimarathon/)

### Chip Timing

Chip timing has been used for the event for the past few years, with great success. This means that everyone gets their own individual finish time. There will be timing gantries at the start and finish lines, so everyone's own individual time begins only when they pass the Start gantry on Centre Park Road, and finishes when they pass the Finish gantry on Monahan Road, adjacent to Kennedy Park.

### Echo Women's Mini Marathon

The Echo Women's Mini Marathon is the biggest event of its kind in Munster. It has grown from its beginnings, in 1982, with only 300 participants, to over 10,000 participants in recent years.

Whether you are a seasoned runner, on a fitness mission, or are joining friends to enjoy the walk, the Mini Marathon is suitable for everyone, with women choosing to run, jog or walk depending on their fitness level.

Each year, several hundred thousand euro is raised for local, national and international charities and organisations. An estimated €1.5 million has been raised for charity by participants over the last three decades, with the participants themselves deciding which charity they will support.

### Charities

Run, jog or walk 5kms for your chosen charity or just for fun. Charities are asked to ensure that all participants fundraising on their behalf are registered to take part in the event. All charitable funds raised by participants are payable directly to the charity concerned.

All profits from the Echo Women's Mini Marathon go directly to Cork County Board of Athletics Ireland, and are used to develop, promote and foster athletics in Cork. All race stewards and officials are unpaid volunteers.

### Prizes and medals

There are prizes for the first 10 female athletes home, presented on the day, plus three prizes in each category, posted out to the winners after the results are finalised. NO RACE NUMBER = NO ENTRY TO THE RACE START AREA & NO MEDAL. Once you cross the finish line you will be directed into Kennedy Park and presented with your medal, where there will also be music and entertainment.

### Safety

- Buggies/prams MUST start at the rear of the field, and you may not run with your buggy
- No dogs in the race (except registered Guide Dogs, or registered Assistance Dogs)
- Children under 13 years of age are not permitted to participate, due to insurance criteria
- Earphones and iPods are not recommended

Approximately 130 stewards and officials are required to manage this event. Medical services are supplied by the Cork Red Cross, St John's Ambulance Brigade, Cork Civil Defence and The Order of Malta, with a doctor on site.

### Runners and wheelchair users

All runners line up on Centre Park Road. Wheelchair participants also assemble here, at the head of the course, and start 15 minutes before the main field, at 12:45pm sharp. Runners line up in time zones according to their own estimated finish times.

Toilets are available in City Hall, with portaloos at the entrance to the start area on Victoria Road, on Mill Road, close to the start area, at Blackrock Village and after the finish area on Monahan Road; wheelchair accessible portaloos are in the start area, in Blackrock Village and after the finish line. Water is available in the finish area only.

events.summary: Lesley Conroy's one-woman retelling of Joyce's The Dead from Gretta Conroy's point of view, after its premiere at the 2026 Bloomsday Festival.
events.description:
Wednesday 23rd to Saturday 26th September @ 8.00pm
plus Matinee Saturday 26th @ 2.30pm

**Presented by tenderfire**

**Epiphany**

Written and performed by Lesley Conroy
Directed by Fiana Toibin

Following the **sold-out**World Premiere at the 2026 Bloomsday Festival, in this bold reimagining of **J****ames Joyce’s ‘The Dead’**, Gretta Conroy takes centre stage at the Misses Morkan’s annual supper party. A night filled with music, dancing and genteel skirmishes.

Gretta has it all: a house by the sea, a gentleman’s family, and a romantic night in The Gresham planned with her dutiful husband Gabriel. But when a love song from her past unearths long-buried memories, Gretta is landed at a crossroads weighing up the choices that shaped her, and the path that lies ahead.

If you are a fan of Joyce and ‘The Dead ’, come and see the story as told from Gretta’s point of view. Gretta gives voice to the preoccupations of mid-life, motherhood and marriage – the secrets you share with your friends in the early hours of the morning.

This unique production expands the female voice in the Joyce canon beyond Molly Bloom, and Nora & Lucia Joyce.

Themes of love, loss and longing are excavated under the ghost weight of the past.

_**Mail on Sunday ******
‘Thrilling Interpretation of Joyce’s Story’.
‘Evocative classic The Dead gets a retelling from a female perspective – and it’s brilliant. Lesley Conroy owns the stage.’_

_**The Reviews Hub ******
Epiphany written and performed by Lesley Conroy and directed by Fiana Toibin encapsulates the perfect character study of Gretta Conroy in James Joyce’s short story “The Dead”._

_**THE ARTS REVIEW ******
‘Conroy conjures an entire world from thin air, seamlessly folding past and present into one another. Delivering with ease the theatrical somersault of a one-woman, multi-character show.’_

**Director:**Fiana Toibin

**Written and Performed by:**Lesley Conroy

**Assistant Director:**Sinead O’Connor Ringwood

**Lighting design:** Cathy O’Carroll

**Set & Costume:** Dara Gill

**Sound**: Brian Dillon

**Music**: Anne-Marie Papin Labazordière

**Choreography:** Muirne Bloomer

**Production images**: Al Craig

_**tenderfire**_ is a new initiative founded by Lesley Conroy that amplifies the female voice in emotionally charged narratives for stage & screen.

_Epiphany was funded by The Arts Council, dlr Arts Grant, dlr Mountain to Sea Bursary, Cork Theatre Collective Space to Play award & Laois Arts Office Tyrone Guthrie Centre Bursary._

events.summary: Hasan Hadi's Caméra d'Or winner, in which a nine-year-old in 1990s Iraq is told to bake a cake for the President's birthday. Opens Cork Cine Club's 30th season, with a glass of wine and cake.
events.description:
[Click here to book online for THE PRESIDENT’S CAKE](https://ie.powertik.com/events/the-president-s-cake-iraq)

**Jamie and Mandy have both seen this film and agreed that it’s perfect for our audience. We’ll serve our customary glass of wine to celebrate the start of our 30th season, and given the film’s subject, there will be cake! **

While people across 1990s Iraq struggle to survive, 9-year old Lamia has been selected to prepare a cake to celebrate the President’s birthday. In a landscape of fear and scarcity, where basic ingredients are nearly impossible to find, Lamia sets out on a determined journey throughout the big city in search of eggs, flour, and sugar. Accompanied by her grandmother, her loyal friend Saeed, and her pet rooster Hindi, she navigates vendors and police officers along the way. *The President’s Cake* is a charming and bitter-sweet crowd-pleaser.

Winner – Caméra d’Or, Cannes Film Festival 2025

*The bonds of the children, Bibi, the postman, and a very few others in their circle endow “The President’s Cake” with a grandly humanistic warmth that’s all the stronger for the mighty pressure under which it’s forged.* – The New Yorker

*This detail-rich and tremendously moving moral fable uncovers harsh realities in Iraqi society without departing from the earnest perspective of its knee-high protagonist, and without diminishing the dignity or value of her hopes and dreams. *– RogerEbert.com

*This is an impressive first feature from the writer-director Hasan Hadi, a sharply observed, bittersweet, child’s-eye odyssey that avoids cute-kid cliches.* – The Observer

*There’s a terrific charm and sweetness in this debut from Iraqi film-maker Hasan Hadi. *– The Guardian

*The President’s Cake is only superficially a story of youthful resilience. The deprivations and darkness of the dictatorship, which immiserates the Iraqi people even as it demands performative displays of happiness, lurk around every corner. *– The New York Times

*At times, the mood is almost larky. (Lamia travels with her cockerel, Hindi, a star.). But the small, grave face of Nayyef — who has never acted before, and gives a great performance — provides the soul of the film. *– Financial Times

[99% Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_presidents_cake)

events.raw:
"Ken O'Sullivan: Stories from the Sea" — Sep 26, 2026, 7:30 PM –
9:10 PM, 15 MacCurtain Street, Victorian Quarter, Cork, T23 E094.
Adult €25.00, Child €20.00, Family €60.00. "In his new show, Stories
from the Sea, award-winning filmmaker Ken O'Sullivan brings us on his
25 year journey exploring the North Atlantic ocean and seas around
Ireland …"
events.summary: The wildlife film-maker's live show on MacCurtain Street: film, stories and 25 years of diving the North Atlantic, from killer whales to blue whales. Family ticket €60.
events.description:
"In his new show, **Stories from the Sea**, award-winning filmmaker Ken
O'Sullivan brings us on his 25 year journey exploring the North
Atlantic ocean and seas around Ireland, with stories, video pieces and
personal insights into his experiences, from being surrounded by a pod
of killer whales to swimming with thousands of dolphins and fin and
blue whales, the largest animals ever to have lived. Ken regales us
with stories of the beauty of the natural world and our emotional
connection with it."

"Ken has now produced more than twenty natural history documentaries
for RTÉ, with his last series North Atlantic acquired by BBC and
broadcast in over 30 countries. He features alongside David
Attenborough in BBC Earth's Stunning Underwater Nature Footage, which
has 7 million views on YouTube."

"The live show is a mix of film and stories from Ken's 20 plus year
long career. He pays homage to his family's 250-year history on Fenit
Island, Co. Kerry and our ancient maritime culture. Education and
conservation have been at the heart of Ken's work since 2005, long
before it was popular to tell stories of damage and even devastation
in natural history documentaries. He will talk about some of the great
challenges facing our marine animals and habitats. Ken has donated his
documentaries to education, where they now feature on the secondary
school exam curriculum within the Junior cycle Geography and Business
Studies courses. His book Stories from the Deep is critically
acclaimed for its lyrical writing and descriptions of nature and
animal encounters, as well as Ken's honesty about his life as a film
maker."

[Click here to book online for BLUE HERON](https://ie.powertik.com/events/blue-heron-canada-hungary)

Vancouver Island in the 1990s. Eight-year-old Sasha’s parents have moved their family from Hungary to Canada. As Sasha and her siblings enjoy the new environment, their parents have become increasingly concerned about the unpredictable behaviour of their eldest son, Jeremy. As the parents desperately try to help their troubled son, Sasha struggles to understand what’s unfolding around her.

★★★★ *Blue Heron juggles painful memoir and self-reflexive film-making with remarkable assurance… A surgically precise and poignant exploration of how families mythologise and editorialise the pain away.* – Irish Times

*A fine-grain family portrait laced with the spirit of documentary reconstruction. It is also hard to write about honestly without sounding like a hype artist, so brilliant is the filmmaking, so startling the narrative depth. *– Financial Times

*Occasionally, a talent arrives fully formed, and the Canadian-Hungarian director Sophy Romvari is one such phenomenon. Already effortlessly fluent in the language of cinema, she is confident enough to have made a feature debut that is entirely her own*. – The Observer

*It’s a reminder of the power of filmmaking to turn the deeply personal into relatable art, and an announcement of a major talent, one who has made the best film of the year to date. *– RogerEbert.com

events.description:
Friday 2nd to Sunday 4th October @ 8.00pm
plus Matinees Saturday and Sunday @ 4.00pm

**GOLL**

Devised by Ensemble
Scripted by Brendan Duffin

Seo taibhléiriú neamhchríochnaithe de chomhar ealaíonta drámatúil dátheangach, **‘Goll’,** idir **Strive Theatre** agus an banna ceoil ó Chorcaigh, **Mac Bóchra.** Is saothar turgnamhach drámaíochta é ‘Goll’, ag sní ceoil, filíochta, scannánaíochta, rince agus scéalaíochta le chéile chun scéalta agus seanchas faoin mBradán Feasa agus ‘Goll Essa Ruadh’ a léiriú. Is ionann Goll Essa Ruadh agus an seanchaí is sine, an t-ilchruthach, Fintan Mac Bóchra.

**Strive Theatre** and Cork band **MacBóchra** present the premiere of their bilingual theatrical collaboration, **GOLL.** An experimental theatre work fusing music, poetry, film, dance, storytelling and spectacle, GOLL, explores the stories and seanchas associated with the salmon of knowledge and Goll Essa Ruadh, the oldest seanchaí and shapeshifter known also as Fintan macBóchra.

Throughout medieval literature Fintan appears as Ireland’s oldest breitheamh and file…a repository of Ireland’s most ancient traditions and stories. Medieval literature depicts him as the sole survivor of the Biblical flood, living on in different forms as sole witness to the various migrations (Partholónian, Nemedian, Fir Bolg, Tuatha Dé Danann, Gael) to Ireland throughout the millennia. Join us as we adapt six medieval narratives associated with Fintan Mac Bóchra into six episodes of contemporary theatre.

_“This experimental theatre experience combines music, dance, poetry and film to delight and surprise at every turn.”_ **– Mikayli Dennehy, The Passage Between.**

_“MacBóchra and Strive embodied the many aspects of the mythical character Fintan. The more I think back on the play, the more vivid and brilliant it becomes – a fantastic performance of dreams and imagination.”_ **– Phillip Spillane, Poet (Audience Member)**

**CAST & CREATIVE TEAM:**

Devised by **Ensemble**

Scripted by **Brendan Duffin**

Directed by **Ciarán MacArtain**

Music by **MacBóchra**

events.description:
[Click here to book online for DEAR YOU](https://ie.powertik.com/events/dear-you-china)

Shot mainly in the Teochew dialect from China’s Guandong region, DEAR YOU follows a cash-strapped grandson who travels to Thailand seeking his billionaire grandfather, only to uncover a decades-old secret about love letters and identity among the mid-century Chinese diaspora.

W**i**th a story that ranges from the 1940s to the present, this generations-spanning drama feels like a good old-fashioned novel, the kind in which coincidences and random accidents cause misunderstandings that last for decades until the truth is finally revealed. Its lashings of period colour and impressive performances has helped to make DEAR YOU a huge box-office hit in the People’s Republic of China.

[Click here](https://www.scmp.com/lifestyle/chinese-culture/article/3357640/how-teochew-people-spread-china-and-their-outsize-influence-hong-kong-thailand)to read an article in the South China Morning Post about DEAR YOU and the Teochew dialect.

[Click here](https://www.screendaily.com/features/dear-you-director-lan-hongchun-talks-inspiration-and-reactions-to-his-chinese-sleeper-hit/5218888.article)to read Screen Daily interview with director Lan Hongchun talking inspiration and reactions to his Chinese sleeper hit.

events.summary: Four days of Irish traditional and folk music in the city's churches, concert halls and Coburg Street pubs, with Altan, Máirtín Ó Connor, Jackie Daly and Matt Cranitch heading the bill and a centenary concert on traditional music on Irish radio. No timetable is published yet.
events.description:
The Cork Folk Festival is preparing for a spectacular 47th edition,
8-11th October, here is a rundown of what to expect.

Headline acts for this year's festival will include: the iconic Donegal
band Altan, featuring fiddler Mairéad Ní Mhaonaigh, Ciarán Curran
(bouzouki), Mark Kelly (guitar), Martin Tourish (accordion) and fiddler
Clare Friel. Ace accordionist Máirtín Ó Connor will feature with Cathal
Hayden and Seamie O' Dowd and Sliabh Luachra's finest, Jackie Daly &
Matt Cranitch will feature again. 'Gals at Play' organised by Mary
Greene will include Mide Houlihan, Aoibheann Carey Philpott, Suzanne
Rowe and Trish Reilly. Breanndán Begley from Baíle na BPoc will arrive
with Cáit Ní Riain on harp and Colm Murphy on bodhran. A historic
concert celebrating 100 years of traditional music on Irish radio will
be curated by Peter Browne featuring an all-star lineup.

Over the festival weekend we will present Lee Valley String Band, Aidan
Coffee, the Noel Brazil Song Contest, a 'Pop Up Céilí', Douglas
Comhaltas, William Jack, Praire Jaywalkers, a concertina gathering, a
fiddle recital, an uilleann pipes concert, a singers circle a Céilí Mór,
music workshops and a walking singing tour. On Sunday of the festival
musicians will gather in Elizabeth Fort for 'Trad in the Fort' and
singer Thomas McCarthy will present a tribute to the late Fermoy
troubadour, Ron Kavana.

The Book 'Reeling down the Years' Cork Folk Festival 1979-2024 by
William Hammond will be on sale over the festival weekend.

The festival is offering a Spáilpín Season Ticket for 65 Euro it
includes all An Spailpín Fánach Concerts.

More details available at cfolkf@gmail.com phone 0872759311.

events.raw: **SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh to host crucial FIFA Women’s World Cup play-off second leg** — Tuesday 13 October 2026, 19:30–22:00. Categories: Key Matches, Live on News, SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh. Tagged: Soccer.
events.summary: The Republic of Ireland women's team play the decisive second leg of their 2027 World Cup qualifying play-off against Kazakhstan on Leeside, back at the ground where they beat the Netherlands 3-2 in June. 19:30 kick-off.
events.description:
SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh is proud to confirm that it will host the **Republic of Ireland Women’s National Team’s decisive second-leg play-off against Kazakhstan** in the **2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup Round One Qualifying Play-Offs** on **Tuesday, October 13th (7.30pm kick-off)**.

The announcement sees the Girls in Green return to the Cork venue that provided the backdrop to one of the most memorable nights in Irish women’s football. In June, a passionate Leeside crowd witnessed a dramatic **3-2 victory over the Netherlands**, sealed by Amber Barrett’s late winner in the 89th minute.

Now, with a place in the next stage of World Cup qualifying at stake, SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh is preparing to welcome another major international occasion to Cork.

The two-legged play-off will begin in **Astana Arena on Friday, October 9th**, before the tie returns to Leeside for what promises to be a thrilling conclusion.

Speaking ahead of the return to Cork, Republic of Ireland Head Coach **Carla Ward** highlighted the impact the supporters made at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh earlier this summer.

“I am delighted to be heading back to Cork. The Netherlands game was incredibly special, particularly because the Cork crowd showed such passion. The supporters turned up in their droves to get behind the team and truly made a difference.

We will need the supporters again as this game is crucial. We cannot take Kazakhstan for granted, especially with the significant travel involved between the two legs. We will need everyone in the stands to get behind the team once more to help us get over the line.”

The electric atmosphere generated by supporters in June showcased SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh as a premier venue for international football, and another large crowd is expected for this crucial October fixture.

### 🎟️ Ticket Information

Tickets for the home leg at **SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh** will go on **pre-sale on August 26th**, with **public sale opening on August 28th at 10am**.

- **Adults:** from €30

- **Children:** from €15

High demand is anticipated following the team’s previous success in Cork.

[Click here to book online for CACTUS PEARS](https://ie.powertik.com/en/events/cactus-pears-india)

Set in rural Maharashtra, Cactus Pears follows Anand, a 30-something Mumbai call-centre worker who returns to his ancestral village to observe the ten-day mourning ritual following his father’s death. While navigating the pressures of family expectations and marriage, he reconnects with Balya, a childhood friend facing similar struggles. Over the course of the mourning period, their bond deepens into a tender and intimate relationship, creating a quiet exploration of grief, identity and queer love within a traditional rural community.

Sundance Film Festival, Winner of Grand Jury Prize in World Cinema Dramatic

*Here is a really impressive directorial debut from Mumbai film-maker Rohan Kanawade: tender, subtle, candid, scrupulously observed.* – The Guardian

*While the film centers on the comfort Anand finds with Balya and vice versa, it is also an elegantly reserved study of Anand’s grief, finding a rhythm in its scenes of ritual that allows us to ache alongside.* – The New York Times

*In less assured hands, Cactus Pears might have edged into trite territory, yielding to the familiar beats of trauma-laden queer love stories, but Kanawade’s considered direction and spare storytelling keep the narrative refreshing. *– The Hollywood Reporter

*A touching queer romance whose subtle rhythms pull us into its tender embrace. *– RogerEbert.com

events.summary: A Bessie Award-winning contemporary dance solo on being read as a foreigner, presented across two nights by the Regional Dance Network.
events.description:
Questioning the notions of place, belonging and otherness

Presented by the Regional Dance Network: Uillinn: West Cork Arts Centre, Dance Limerick, Tipperary Dance and Dance Cork Firkin Crane.

Wanjiru Kamuyu is engaged in questioning the notions of place, belonging and otherness. A cosmopolitan on three continents - Africa, North America and Europe – wherever she decides to set up home, is she considered an immigrant?

Her solo interrogates the gaze upon the “foreigner” in a new space, new society. The work, through satire, offers a critical eye on the notions of place and placement that are prevalent in today’s political discourse. An Immigrant’s Story is a Bessie Award winner in the category Outstanding Choreographer.

WKcollective creates immersive, visceral experiences through the medium of contemporary dance. Project-based works weave stories and express universal experiences. Collaboration across artistic disciplines opens discourse and intrigue through the power of poetic expression in vocal and physical movement. Founded by Kenyan-American choreographer Wanjiru Kamuyu in 2009, WKcollective attracts multidisciplinary artists of diverse cultural backgrounds to the creative canvas. Drawing upon these art forms to stimulate fresh, innovative, vulnerable, raw, graphic art to generate personal and social reflection through a transformative celebration with dance.

Wanjiru Kamuyu holds an MFA from Temple University and began her career in New York with Urban Bush Women and Molissa Fenley. She has collaborated with artists including Bill T. Jones, Robyn Orlin, Bartabas, Irène Tassembedo, and Anne Collod amongst others. Since 2017, Kamuyu has created several works presented across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the US, as well as a dance film, La Visite (2020).

events.raw: **Munster Rugby set for fourth appearance at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh** — Saturday 17 October 2026 at 8pm. Categories: Key Matches, Live on News, Match Centre, SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh. Tagged: Munster Rugby.
events.summary: Munster open their 2026/27 Investec Champions Cup campaign against Racing 92 at Páirc Uí Chaoimh, their fourth rugby outing at the stadium and one they have never lost. 20:00 kick-off.
events.description:
SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh is preparing to welcome Munster Rugby for a **fourth time**, with Racing 92 set to provide the opposition when the province opens its 2026/27 Investec Champions Cup campaign in Cork on **Saturday, October 17th at 8pm**.

Since hosting its first-ever rugby match in November 2022, SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh has quickly established itself as a spectacular venue for major rugby occasions, with Munster having won all three of their previous matches at the stadium.

### A memorable rugby history

The story began on **10 November 2022**, when Munster faced a touring South Africa A side in the first rugby match ever played at Páirc Uí Chaoimh.

A remarkable **41,400 supporters** attended the historic fixture, setting a record for attendance at a rugby match in the province of Munster.

The crowd was rewarded with a memorable performance as Munster ran out **28-14 winners**.

Just over a year later, Munster returned to Cork for another major international rugby occasion.

On **3 February 2024**, the province faced New Zealand Super Rugby giants the Crusaders in a sold-out clash in front of **40,885 supporters**.

Another dramatic contest followed, with Munster edging to a **21-19 victory**.

The stadium then welcomed its first competitive European rugby fixture when Munster hosted Gloucester in the Investec Champions Cup on **13 December 2025**.

In front of **36,208 supporters**, Munster produced a commanding performance to defeat the English side **31-3**, securing a bonus-point victory and setting a record attendance for a Champions Cup game in Munster.

### Fourth time around

Now, Munster are set to return to SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh for a **fourth appearance**, bringing the Investec Champions Cup back to Cork for another major European occasion.

French Top 14 side **Racing 92** will provide the opposition in Round 1 of the competition, with kick-off scheduled for **8pm on Saturday, October 17th**.

Across Munster’s three previous appearances, more than **118,000 supporters** have passed through the gates of SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh.

With the venue having already witnessed victories over South Africa A, the Crusaders and Gloucester, another chapter in the stadium’s growing rugby history will be written when Racing 92 arrive on Leeside.

events.description:
Rebel Run 5k & 10k Road Races 2026

MTU, Bishopstown, Cork. 9:30am, Sunday October 18th 2026.

This event is run under an Athletics Ireland permit/licence. Organised and hosted by Leisureworld Bishopstown & Cork Sports Partnership, in association with sponsors and supporters. These courses were measured by John Quigley, AIMS/World Athletics International Grade A Measurer.

- [Rebel Run website](http://www.rebelrun.ie)
- [Leisureworld Bishopstown website](http://bishopstown.leisureworldcork.com/)
- [Cork Sports Partnership website](http://www.corksports.ie/)
- [Register Here](https://eventmaster.ie/event/PkpYsJDhLe)

There will be limited sign-in on the morning, between 8am and 9am. Parking is available in both MTU and Leisureworld car parks.

Please pin your event number to the front, and mark clearly on the reverse your emergency contact number, along with any medical conditions that should be declared.

Headphones may NOT be worn — roads are open to traffic, therefore, for safety, everyone must be able to hear marshal instructions, and traffic, at all times.

The event starts at 9.45am sharp, from the back of the MTU athletics stand (please note new start areas from previous years). The race will finish on the MTU running track, where light refreshments will be provided. Medical support will be provided by the Irish Red Cross.

Chip timing. Souvenir T-shirt. AAI licence and measured by Jones Counter. 5k event open to those 16+.

### Rebel Run 5k

The 5k start line is towards the southwestern end on the lower tier of the carpark. Both routes begin in MTU, but at slightly different locations, and continue on the same route until Rossbrook Estate, where the 5k runners are directed towards the Curraheen Walkway and along by the rugby and GAA pitches at the back of MTU.

The route follows the pathway until directed to take a left towards the tennis club, then returns onto the pathway, passing the Pitch and Putt Club and on for another 0.5k, before turning left at approx. 3k and left again, passing the tennis courts. Runners again pass the Pitch and Putt Club before exiting onto the road by Elton Lawn, followed by a left turn onto Rossa Avenue. The route enters the MTU campus through the first gate on Rossa Avenue, swings sharply left around the southern side of the campus, then swings left into the track by the 200m line and finishes at the normal finish line on the track.

events.description:
**The Blue Mist 2026 – Reimagined at The Pav!**

We're back with a brand-new seated show, perfect for all ages — a powerful night of music, dance, and culture!

Live music by Daniel Viledo and Benjamín Becerra. All-new choreography and storytelling. Stunning re-mastered visuals. A vibrant tribute to Día de los Muertos.

This year marks 12 years of Mexican folk dance in Ireland, and we're proud to support Fundación Freedom in Mexico with part of our profits.

Family-friendly. Seating is available but not assigned and is limited. Book your tickets now!

We're returning for the forth year with a brand-new show — and this time, we're diving into the stories and traditions behind Día de los Muertos. Through powerful dance, live music, and bold visuals, we'll bring this celebration to life and share how it's been honoured in Mexico for generations.

This night isn't just about performance — it's about connection, culture, and celebration. Expect great music, proper dancing, wonderful people, and a vibrant atmosphere.

We're also marking 12 years of dancing Mexican folk in Ireland. Come along, bring your friends, and be part of a night that means something.

events.description:
[Click here to book online for PRIMAVERA](https://ie.powertik.com/en/events/primavera-italy)

An astounding feature debut by the acclaimed Italian opera director, Damiano Michieletto, set in early 18th century Venice. Renowned for its exceptional music programme, the Pièta orphanage is home to Cecilia, a young violin virtuoso. Despite her talent, Cecilia’s future seems dim, with the prospect of an arranged marriage her only hope of escape. Her life changes drastically when Antonio Vivaldi, a brilliant and ambitious composer, arrives as the new music teacher. Through a complex artistic relationship with Vivaldi and his music, Cecilia finds the strength to challenge the destiny that once seemed inevitable.

*The dark, atmospheric tone of the film is enhanced by an engrossing storyline and a brilliant acting performance by Tecla Insolia. Primavera announces Damiano Michieletto as a filmmaker to watch.* – Subculture Entertainment

*Insolia and Riondino are quite perfectly cast. Their characters have soul chemistry and their scenes together are the film’s best.* – The Times [UK]

events.summary: Sofia Coppola-produced adaptation of Alysia Abbott's memoir of growing up with a gay poet father in 1970s San Francisco.
events.description:
[Click here to book online for FAIRYLAND](https://ie.powertik.com/en/events/fairyland-usa)

In this poignant adaptation of Alysia Abbott’s memoir, produced by Sofia Coppola, a daughter is along for the ride of her young life when her widowed father heads west to 1970s San Francisco to claim his authentic self in the exhilarating early days of gay liberation. Amiable, well-meaning Steve is a queer poet trying to balance fatherhood and writing with his enthusiastic exploration of his sexuality. Eight-year-old Alysia is rolling with life’s changes and watching the Pride parade go by.

The older Alysia reveals more complicated emotions as a young woman struggling to come to terms with her bohemian upbringing and sometimes irresponsible father. First-time director Andrew Durham captures the heady sense of freedom and possibility of an era along with the shattering reality of AIDS as it sweeps in, destroying lives and upending community.

*This fond, wise, lived-in film chronicles a spectrum of parentification – with the parties switching roles – over turbulent decades. Its emotional force is found in the two-step between parent and child as the sweep of LGBTQ+ history catches up.* – The Irish Times

*Andrew Durham’s adaptation of the bestselling Alysia Abbott memoir is a fine debut for the writer-director, one that mines ache and beauty within this most novel inflection of the father-daughter dynamic.* – Irish Independent

*Durham’s direction is sensitive and assured, and he does a great job mixing his location work with archival footage to create an authentic sense of what San Francisco was like during those times.* – San Francisco Chronicle

*An honest, real movie about people living big lives during tumultuous times, and coming through it damaged but wiser.* – RogerEbert.com

*At its most thoughtful, “Fairyland” conveys a dual sense of loss — spanning personal loves and lovers, and whole historical moments and communities — in such small, sweet gestures as a head on a shoulder, a hand in a hand, a silence finally understood.* – Variety

[96% Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/fairyland)

events.summary: Akinola Davies Jr's Cannes-winning debut: two brothers spend a day in 1993 Lagos with their absent father. Shown with an Irish short.
events.description:
Click here to book online for MY FATHER’S SHADOW

Set over one day in 1993 Nigeria, young bothers Remi and Akin are taken by surprise when their often-absent father Folarin arrives home. Their surprise turns into excitement when Folarin suggests that the brothers accompany him to Lagos for the day, as he needs to collect a long-overdue salary. The trip becomes a journey of discovery for the boys as they spend time with their father and become more aware of their country’s political unrest. Drawing loosely on his own experiences and co-written with his brother, this first feature from director Akinola Davies Jr. deftly explores themes of loss, memory, nostalgia and connected histories.

*[My Father’s Shadow] quietly marries personal and national histories, offering a deceptively sprawling portrait of Lagos, a family and the fragile, frantic ways people try to hold on against tyranny.*– The Irish Times

★★★★* In his Cannes-winning feature debut, the British-Nigerian filmmaker has crafted something quite special, and nails that elusive trick of finding the universal in the particular.* *– *The Irish Independent

*The casting is inspired… And Dìrísù’s tender, thoughtful, strong presence — his face often framed in the tightest of close-ups — evokes Folarin’s virtues as a father and a man, as well as his imperfections.* – Financial Times

*This terrific semi-autobiographical first feature from filmmaker Akinola Davies Jr, which stars Gangs of London’s Sope Dirisu as the boys’ magnetic father Folarin, is a thrillingly vital account of the moment when everything changes. *– Screen International

*This is an enchanting film. At every moment, one feels spellbound by its earnest aims and its heart-warming excursions.* – RogerEbert.om

*It is a rich, heartfelt and rewarding movie.* – The Guardian

*It’s that sharp contrast of beauty with an undercurrent of pain that makes “My Father’s Shadow” so bittersweet, and it’s why it cuts to the quick.* – The New York Times

*My Father’s Shadow is a gem, a deeply felt memory piece and vibrant portrait of Nigeria in 1993.* – Associated Press

[98% Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/my_fathers_shadow)

events.description:
[Click here to book online for HEN](https://ie.powertik.com/events/hen-greece)

Told entirely from the perspective of its feathered protagonist, HEN follows a chicken who escapes an industrial farm only to find herself navigating the pecking order of a crumbling seaside restaurant in Greece. As she fights to protect her eggs, she becomes an unwitting witness to the complex human lives around her as the restaurant is caught up in greed, smuggling, and the migrant crisis. Eight chickens play the lead character.

[Click here](https://variety.com/2025/film/global/gyorgy-palfi-toronto-platform-title-hen-1236512055/) to read Variety article: ”György Pálfi Talks Logistical Challenges of Working With Eight Chicken Protagonists in HEN”

*Mundane routines acquire a creeping dread, with barns, kitchens and farmyards becoming landscapes of unspoken terror as the heroine clucks her way through a compelling story.* – The Irish Times

*A wild, surreal, harrowing and funny ride that may even win you over to veganism. Think Chicken Run for intellectuals.*  – Empire Magazine

Cork College of FET, Douglas Street Campus. Tickets €8.50 / €7 concession. Online booking closes at 18:30 on the night of the film; pay at the door by card or cash if not sold out online.
events.summary: The season's Classic Film Choice: Chabrol's 1968 study of a husband, an affair and a quiet act of revenge.
events.description:
[Trailer with English subtitles not available.]

[Click here to book online for LA FEMME INFIDELE](https://ie.powertik.com/events/classic-film-la-femme-infidele-france-1968)

This season’s Classic Film Choice is – after much debate by your committee! – LA FEMME INFIDELE [The Unfaithful Wife].

A 1968 masterpiece from Claude Chabrol’s remarkable run of bourgeois psychological thrillers, La Femme infidèle traces the fallout following a husband’s discovery of his wife’s affair and his quiet, unnerving and devastating act of revenge. Dubbed the ‘French Hitchcock’, Chabrol’s career spanned some 50 years and 80-odd films. Few directors have mapped the darkness beneath respectable surfaces with his wit, precision and relentless productivity.

*What could have been just another thriller becomes much more than that. It is also a passionate love story, with its share of intense irony and a pervading sense of the quirkiness of fate.* – The Guardian

*A brilliantly ambivalent scrutiny of bourgeois marriage and murder that juggles compassion and cynicism in a way that makes Hitchcock look obvious.* – *Time Out*

**LA FEMME INFIDELE** **[The Unfaithful Wife]**

France, 1968 | Language: French | 1 hr 38 min | Cert:

Director: Claude Chabrol

Cast: Stéphane Audran and Michel Bouquet

Foreign language films are subtitled.

occurrence.pattern: Semester Two — course commences Tuesday 19th January 2027, from 6.30pm - 9.00pm

events.venueName: MTU Crawford College of Art & Design
events.raw:
**Ceramics: Bringing Your Ideas to Life** — When: Semester Two: Course
commences Tuesday 19th January 2027, from 6.30pm - 9.00pm. Course
Registration Opens: 1st December 2026. Course Application Deadline:
15th January 2027. Course Fee: €400. Tutor: Bernadette Tuite.

"This course offers the student the opportunity to realise his/her
ideas through the medium of clay."
events.summary: The self-directed end of the ceramics ladder: you set your own project and develop it in clay through handbuilding, with group critiques across the semester and basic slip, underglaze and glaze decoration.
events.description:
This course offers the student the opportunity to realise his/her
ideas through the medium of clay. The student engages in the process of
creative idea development and the production of selected pieces using
handbuilding techniques. Students set their own project and develop
their ideas using both their visual notebooks and practical
handbuilding skills. Students are encouraged to engage with more
self-generated projects that reflect their individual interests. The
course explores the application of basic decoration using slips,
underglazes and glazing. There will be a number of group analysis and
discussion sessions to review progress throughout the year. The course
explores the appropriate criteria and visual grammar for reading and
interpreting ceramic artefacts and students are encouraged to apply
these to their own work also.

events.raw:
**Ocean to City is on 5 June 2027.** "Are you ready for the challenge?
Ireland's premier multi craft race."

"This year's Ocean to City - An Rás Mór has come to a close. Thank you
to everyone who made this year's race such a success. While we look
ahead to next year's Ocean to City on 5 June 2027 - why not keep rowing
and paddling with our 5 Miles from Home challenge?"

"Ocean to City – An Rás Mór is Ireland's very own long-distance rowing
race attracting hundreds of participants annually. Started in 2005, it
has grown from its origin as a race for traditional fixed-seat boats
into an all-inclusive rowing and paddling event, embracing everything
from traditional wooden working boats, currachs, skiffs, gigs and
longboats to contemporary ocean racing shells, kayaks, canoes and even
stand-up paddle boards."
events.summary: Ireland's largest multi-craft rowing and paddling race, hundreds of boats of every kind pulling from Crosshaven up Cork Harbour to the quays in the city centre. Free to watch from the quaysides and the anchor event of Cork Harbour Festival.

events.description:
**BIND** is a programme of exhibitions of individual artist books as
part of Cork Printmakers artist book library.

The first exhibition presents the artist book *Ink Drawing Series I*
by Eimearjean McCormack. The book is hand printed and hand bound by
McCormack and includes a selection of ink drawings, risograph prints
and screenprints.

The creation of limited-edition books and experimental publications
have become an integral extension of Eimearjean's printmaking
practice. For her, the book format generates space for further
exploration, functioning simultaneously as an archive of process and
as a platform for new ideas to emerge.

**BIND** aims to celebrate contemporary book art in printmaking
through exhibiting artist books by three invited artists and groups
within our existing library and archive of printmakers artist books
across 2026. The programme will activate the existing library and
celebrate the new and innovative approaches to artists books as a both
social and intimate durational art object.

**Bind Programme 2026**

- June/July: Eimearjean Mc Cormack
- September: Elize de Beer
- October: Cork Zine Fest

Opening times 10am-4pm Monday - Thursday or by appointment. Closed for
lunch 1pm-2pm. To avoid disappointment, please note that the gallery
may occasionally be closed during these hours due to annual leave or
offsite work. We recommend calling or emailing in advance to arrange
an appointment.

"Cork City Food History Tour takes you on a 2-hour walking tour of the city center
with food tastings along the way. We visit the English Market and the Butter
Museum, with stops for tasting and chat. A walking tour of Cork city with
commentary on the food and drinks history of the city going back to Viking days.
See where the merchants lived and traded in times past as the city developed from
the confines of its medieval walls."

"Tours Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday at 10.00 am to 12.00."
"Min 2 per booking. Group tours by arrangement."
"Fitness Level 2 | Guided Tour | Food Tour | Medium Demand Tour | 2 Hours"

Three different prices are printed for it across two pages of this site and the festival programme, so no figure is asserted here.
events.description:
"Under the fun and insightful guidance of local food expert, chef, home economics
teacher and native Irish speaker, Maire Ní Mhurchu, learn about Cork's food
heritage and how it has developed over the past 300 years. During a walking tour
of this maritime city, you will visit the Butter Museum where you will learn the
history of Irish Butter, known as 'yellow gold', the story of Butter Roads to Cork
and the other foods produced in the breadbasket of Ireland.

Finish the tour with a stop at the iconic English Market. Meet some of the key
traders while collecting samples of delicious local produce at 4 different stalls
including cheeses, and fish, to taste along the route."

Optional extras, pre-ordered: "1. Sandwich from the English Market pre-ordered
with some of the amazing food of the market. Choice of 4 Flavours – from Spiced
Beef, Vegetarian or Cheese per sandwich €9.50 each. 2. Gluten-Free Food option
with Gluten-free picnic box for 1 person €35pp. 3. A picnic box for 2 people of 3
local cheese, bread, traditional spiced beef, olives, cake for a picnic. Get the
real flavor of Cork city €35pp."

occurrence.pattern: Tastings generally take place on Wednesdays and there is no set start time – you can basically join us anytime between 5.30pm and 8.00pm

events.raw:
**GUERRILLA TASTINGS**

"Our Guerrilla Tastings are informal pop-up tastings – arranged at a moment's
notice – a bit like a flashmob event.

Born during a time when outdoor dining was all we had and the weather played a
huge part. When we saw the weather was going to be good, we'd pop-up on the
terrace for an informal tasting, pouring flights of wine along a given theme.
These tastings proved to be so popular, that we've decided to continue them on
indoors, keeping that nature of surprise and spontaneity.

Here's how they work: we pour a flight of wines and serve accompanying bites to
match. These aren't formal tutored tastings. We leave you to your own devices
to enjoy the drinks, but give a brief explanation of each wine. The perfect way
to catch up with your friends! Tastings generally take place on Wednesdays and
there is no set start time – you can basically join us anytime between 5.30pm
and 8.00pm."
events.summary: The wine bar's standing informal pop-up tasting — a themed flight with bites to match, drop in any time between half five and eight, usually on a Wednesday. Themed editions are announced individually as they come up.

events.description:
"Our tour guides, who are self-confessed beer nerds, will briefly bring you
through Ireland's rich brewing history and explain how our family-owned and
independently run brewery fits into Ireland's current thriving beer scene.

We will introduce you to a simplified science behind making beer and introduce
you to each of the different vessels and how they're used in our custom-built
brewery.

From the brewery we move to the bar to take you through a guided beer tasting
where we introduce you to the Rising Sons' award-winning brews, and offer you
an opportunity to learn a little bit about identifying different beer styles as
well as giving you a chance to tell us what you think!

Finally, we round up the tour with a quick Question & Answers session where
we'll do our utmost to answer any questions you've ever had about beer, the art
of making it and indeed drinking it!

If you can't make it to one of our tours, never fear! You can still sample the
best the Rising Sons has to offer at our brewpub and many great venues across
the country."

events.description:
This unique course offers a chance to enter Third Level as a part-time
student to concentrate on textiles as an expressive medium within an
Art College environment.

What will you be doing? This is a two year course: Year One integrates
lectures and seminars (Mondays) with textiles studio (each Tuesday).
Year One is a balance between essays, discussions, and presentations
with the technical challenges of the broad range of textile techniques
presented (stitch/print/weave/felt/paper/3d/basketry). In the second
Semester, studio projects challenge creative investigation and research
toward finished works around project themes. In Year Two only the
Tuesday studio course is held, and is grounded in weekly group research
discussions and seminars presenting samples and works in progress for
feedback and development. Individuality and innovation are encouraged
as final works evolve toward exhibition presentation. As a bonus,
additional textiles research challenges entered alongside fulltime
Applied Art students provide opportunities to exhibit both in the city
and internationally.

Why do this course?

- It provides a structured and thorough immersion in textile making and
  textile culture, balancing studio and academic challenges.
- It nurtures the research development of individual artistic languages
  in textiles, in the context of contemporary fine art and applied art
  practice.
- It forms a supportive and inspiring peer group of like-minded textile
  makers, taught by senior lecturing staff of the MTU Crawford who also
  teach on the fulltime Fine Art and Applied Art Degree.
- It offers project involvement and exhibition opportunities shared
  alongside the fulltime Contemporary Applied Arts Degree, such as
  recent exchange projects with Estonian and Lithuanian textile
  departments.

Cork's covered municipal market, trading on the same site since 1788 and

fishmongers, butchers, cheesemongers, bakers and spice stalls under one
roof, open six mornings a week, with cafés and food counters upstairs.
events.description:
"Discover a vibrant and diverse marketplace, where an eclectic mix of
traders come together. Nestled alongside long-standing family-run stalls
passed down through generations, our market offers the best in local
produce. From fresh meats and fish to herbs, spices, fruits, vegetables,
sauces, oils, chocolates, cakes, cheeses, and pastas — there's something
to suit all taste buds and occasions."

"The market offers visitors unique finds including crockery, T-shirts,
novelty items, clothing alterations, and local art. This diverse
selection creates a lively atmosphere that reflects the market's
character and charm."

"Immerse yourself in the sights, sounds, and aromas of the market, then
relax and savor the flavors at our welcoming cafés, delis, and food
stalls."

Traders are grouped as: Bakery & Confectionery; Food for Now;
Delicatessen; Fish & Seafood; Fruit and Veg; Meat, Poultry and Game;
Spices, Preserves and Condiments; Specialities; Wine.

**Where it is.** "The English Market is located in Cork city centre with
its main entrances on Grand Parade, and on Princes Street, with further
smaller entrances off Oliver Plunkett Street and Patrick Street."

**Visiting.** "To ensure that tourists and casual visitors to the English
Market can get the maximum from their visit, tour groups are encouraged
to come outside of peak trading hours. In general, the busier trading
hours of 11.00 am – 4.30 pm daily should be avoided (Friday and Saturday
can be particularly hectic)." Tour groups are asked to register in
advance. Public toilet facilities are limited to one coin-operated toilet
near the fish aisle.

**Why the name.** "The Market was created in 1788 by the Protestant or
'English' corporation that controlled the city until 1841... When local
government was reformed in 1840, and the representatives of the city's
Catholic, 'Irish' majority took over, they established another covered
food market, St. Peter's (now the Bodega@St Peter's Market) which became
known as the 'Irish Market'."

**Who runs it.** "Cork City Council owns the English Market and leases
the stalls to traders. Cork City Council contracts with Lisney who look
after the day-to-day running of the market."

Payment: "Some traders accept credit cards and laser cards, however many
traders deal on a cash-only basis."

events.description:
Mahon Point Farmers' Market is the largest Farmers Market Cork has to
offer, bringing together a diverse range of local farmers and artisan food
producers in one large weekly market held outside the main entrance of
Mahon Point Shopping Centre every Thursday morning from 10am to 2pm.

Established in 2006, Mahon Point Farmers' Market has over 50 stalls of
high-quality foods available, much of it organic, lovingly grown, produced
or sourced by small producers across the county. The market has won an
array of prestigious awards including the Good Food Ireland "Best Farmers
Market Award" and the McKennas Guide "Best in Ireland" Award.

**Sustainability**

Our vision for our weekly Farmers Market is to be as plastic free as
possible and fully sustainable. We believe in local food systems and the
majority of our stallholders grow, rear, catch or bake their produce within
an hour's drive of Mahon Point reducing food miles and providing the
freshest food.

We are currently developing a project with CUSP (Cork Urban Soil Project)
where all of our compostable market waste will be broken down in a bio
digester and turned into soil that will then be distributed to gardens and
growing projects around the city.

**Awards**

The market has won an array of prestigious awards including the Good Food
Ireland "Best Farmers Market Award" and the McKennas Guide "Best in
Ireland" Award 2008, 2009, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017. In 2018,
it won Best Farmers Market in Cork at the #96fmbestofcork awards with
Cork's 96FM and The KC Show.

For all market inquiries please contact: Rupert Hugh-Jones at
farm@rossmoreoysters.com or on 086 1685312.

"Wilton Market takes the ethos of organic, locally sourced and seasonal very

Farmers Market, Wilton Shopping Centre, Cork. +353 86 168 5312.
events.summary:
One of the larger suburban farmers' markets — over forty-five stalls in the
grounds of Wilton Shopping Centre out by the hospital and the university —
trading midweek, though which day is not stated anywhere I could reach.
events.description:
With over 45 regular stalls serving up everything from burritos to locally
produced artisan meats, cheeses and veg, this busy market in the grounds of
a shopping centre in the suburb of Wilton is a great mid-week option -
especially if you want to stock up before heading to West Cork.

The Market gives customers a diverse range of naturally produced foods and
connects local producers and farmers to the public and restaurateurs in an
atmosphere that fosters community and fun.

"Wilton Market takes the ethos of organic, locally sourced and seasonal very
seriously."

Farmers Market, Wilton Shopping Centre, Cork.

events.title: Alien Worlds
events.timesText: Open Monday to Sunday 10.00 - 18:00, last entry 17.00, no booking required
events.raw:
**Alien Worlds**

There are worlds out there beyond the horizon of our own solar system. Let's
explore them together...

Exoplanets are planets that orbit stars outside our own solar system. Our
capacity to document and study them is still relatively new, but with recent
advancements in the field we have seen an exponential increase in the number
of worlds we know of. These planets exist far beyond anything we can see in
detail with even our most advanced optical telescopes, but through absolutely
ingenious scientific methods we have already learned a great deal about these
alien worlds.
events.summary: How you find a planet you cannot see - transits, wobbles and spectra - and what the exoplanet catalogue now says about the odds of anything living out there.

events.title: Ireland in Space
events.timesText: Open Monday to Sunday 10.00 - 18:00, last entry 17.00, no booking required
events.raw:
**Permanent Exhibition — Ireland in Space**

From Newgrange to New Space - Ireland's connection to Space may be deeper than
you think...

From our earliest days, the Irish people have had an abiding connection to the
stars. Our Stone Age ancestors built monuments that tracked the Sun, while more
recent ancestors pioneered fields of mathematics that proved integral to the
Apollo 11 Moon landing. Irish scientists have made their mark on the world
history of astronomy and exploration, but our future looks even brighter. As
Irish scientists at the European Space Agency work on the next generation of
Space exploration, Irish businesses are beginning to reap the rewards that the
New Space industry has to offer.
events.summary: The observatory's standing exhibition on Ireland's stake in space, running from Newgrange's solar alignments through Hamilton's quaternions to what Irish firms are currently building for the European Space Agency.

events.raw:
**Castle & Gardens Open All Year Round!** Explore the entire gardens, mystical
rock close, dungeons, caves, lake walk & much more!

Welcome to Blarney Castle, the home of the Blarney Stone. Built nearly six
hundred years ago by one of Ireland's greatest chieftans, Cormac MacCarthy, and
has been attracting attention ever since. Over the last few hundred years,
millions have flocked to Blarney making it a world landmark and one of
Ireland's greatest treasures.

Buy tickets in advance online or at our ticket office on arrival. We do not
have timed slots.
events.summary: Cormac MacCarthy's 1440s tower house, the stone at the top of it, and the sixty acres most visitors underrate - the Rock Close, the poison garden, the caves and the lake walk. Open every day but Christmas, hours shifting by month.

price.text: Adults €5.00; Students/Seniors/Concession €4.00; Children €2.00; children under 12 free in a family group; carers/accompanying persons free; groups (10+) by arrangement

events.raw:
**Welcome to The Butter Museum — An Original and Memorable Experience**

The Butter Museum is a unique institution, celebrating one of the great
success stories of Ireland, the butter trade. Located in the historic
Shandon area of Cork city, the story begins with the central role of dairy
culture in the Island of Saints and Scholars. The Museum goes on to describe
the internationally important Butter Exchange in nineteenth century Cork,
the traditional craft of home butter making and the modern success of the
Kerrygold brand.
events.summary: A small self-guided museum in Shandon on how butter made Cork rich - the nineteenth-century Butter Exchange, the craft of home butter-making, and the invention of Kerrygold - with a wrapper collection and a film.

events.title: Butter Making Demonstrations
events.raw:
**Butter Making Demonstrations** — Experience the Art of Traditional Butter
Making on Wednesdays and Saturdays at 12.00.

We are a small Museum and can only seat 35 guests for our butter making
demonstrations. We cannot offer a pre-payment or booking facility for
demonstrations: to increase your chances of a seat, we recommend you arrive
early at 11 am or thereabouts, enjoy the Museum self-guided tour and stay for
the demonstration. If all seats are taken by 11.40 am or so, we may go ahead
with the demonstration. There is always plenty of fresh bread and newly-made
butter to sample afterwards even if you missed the demonstration this time!
events.summary: Traditional hand butter-making twice a week, 35 seats, no booking - turn up around 11 and do the museum first. Fresh bread and new butter to taste afterwards either way.

events.title: SUFFERING THE MOST–Tomas MacCurtain and Terence MacSwiney
events.raw:
**SUFFERING THE MOST–Tomas MacCurtain and Terence MacSwiney**

SUFFERING THE MOST – The life and times of Tomas McCurtain and Terence
MacSwiney.
events.summary: A standing exhibition on the two republican Lord Mayors of Cork who died in 1920 - MacCurtain shot at his home in March, MacSwiney on hunger strike in Brixton in October - built around the museum's own collection and loans from the MacSwiney family. No start or end date is printed.

Step into history and loads of fun at Nano Nagle Place, a welcoming stop on
Cork's Playful Culture Trail. Explore our beautiful gardens, historic
buildings, and museum as you follow the trail, collect your stamp, and take on

events.title: Illuminating Justice: Voices of Change Exhibition

price.text: Nano Nagle Place Museum (paid admission); free online

events.raw:
**Illuminating Justice: Voices of Change Exhibition** — 2025 -2026 | Nano
Nagle Place Museum (paid admission) | Free Online.
events.summary: Nano Nagle as an eighteenth-century agitator rather than a saint, set beside present-day voices from the site's own community projects. Runs across 2025-26 with no closing date given; there is a free online version.
events.description:
2025 -2026 | Nano Nagle Place Museum (paid admission) | Free Online

Step into the story of Nano Nagle, a fearless trailblazer whose passion for
justice and education transformed lives in 18th-century Ireland.
"Illuminating Justice: Voices of Change" brings her legacy to life, showing
how one woman's vision sparked a movement that still inspires action today.

Discover how Nano Nagle Place continues to shine as a beacon of hope,
empowering communities and championing social justice in the heart of Cork. Be
inspired by voices of change—past and present—and see how you, too, can be
part of this ongoing journey. This exhibition celebrates her legacy and shows
how her vision continues to inspire change today.

Supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport.

events.title: Spike Island Literary Festival

occurrence.note: The listing and the festival's own page say only "returns this September" and "Join us at the Spike Island Literary Festival this September" - no dates anywhere, and the digitickets shop lists it as a product without a date either.

events.raw:
**Spike Island Literary Festival** — Now in its fifth year, the Spike Island
Literary Festival returns this September with a gripping programme dedicated to
the art of crime writing.
events.summary: A crime-writing festival held inside a former convict prison, fifth year - panels, readings in the cells, and a literary agent taking pitches. Mark Billingham, Andrea Mara, Stuart Neville and Catherine Ryan Howard are named; the dates are not.
events.description:
Now in its fifth year, the Spike Island Literary Festival returns this September
with a gripping programme dedicated to the art of crime writing.

Set against the unique backdrop of Spike Island's infamous former prison, this
one-of-a-kind festival brings together world-renowned authors and literary
experts for a series of thrilling conversations, live readings and
thought-provoking panels.

With a dark history of four prisons over 400 years, Spike Island is the perfect
setting for literary enthusiasts from book lovers to budding writers. Engage with
your favourite authors and discover what inspires them through author-led panel
discussions, experience readings from world-class writers as they recite their
most famous works in unique locations or take the first steps to getting your own
work published by meeting with a renowned literary agent.

Step inside the walls that once held some of Ireland's most notorious criminals
and immerse yourself in stories that intrigue, unnerve and captivate. Whether
you're a fan of psychological thrillers, gritty detective fiction, or chilling
true crime, Spike Island is the ultimate setting for your next plot twist.

This year's programme features a stellar line-up of renowned authors such as Mark
Billingham, Andrea Mara, Stuart Neville, Catherine Ryan Howard and more.

Writers named on the page: Mark Billingham, Sam Blake, Edel Coffey, Clare
Coughlan, PJ Coogan, Michelle Dunne, Fiona Gartland, Amy Jordan, Andrea Mara,
Stuart Neville, Mercier Press, Michelle McDonagh, Kitty Murphy, Gill Perdue,
Cormac Quinn, Catherine Ryan Howard, R.O. Throp, Mary Watson.

events.title: Cork City Walks guided city walk

occurrence.note: No schedule, dates, days or times are published anywhere on the site's four pages; the page's own timestamp is 2022-07-12. The route is described but never scheduled.

events.raw:
**Céad Míle Fáilte — A Hundred Thousand Welcomes!**

Welcome to Cork City Walks. We look forward to meeting you on one of our friendly, informative,
leisurely walks around our beautiful and charming city.

We encourage interaction and banter as we seek to share with you our love of Cork, its unique history,
friendly people, colourful culture and Corkonian wit and traditions. We will take you on a leisurely
walk around the compact 800 year old city, where you will experience the smells and sounds of the
English Market, stroll the busy lanes of the 18th century Huguenot Quarter and wonder at Burges's
magnificent French Neo-Gothic cathedral.
events.summary: A leisurely guided walk of the compact medieval city taking in the English Market, the Huguenot Quarter and St Fin Barre's Cathedral. Real, and completely unscheduled — no dates, days, times or public price are published.

**When is it?** It is held every Sunday at 9:30am.

**Where is it?** The event takes place at Nursery Drive Park, Nursery Drive, Ballinlough, Cork.

**What does it cost to join in?** Nothing - it's free! but please register before you first come along. Only ever register with parkrun once and don't forget to bring a scannable copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

**How fast do I have to be?** The aim is to have fun. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

All parkrun events are organised by volunteers — email nurserydrivejuniors@parkrun.com to help.

occurrence.pattern: Sessions are Thursday, Friday and Saturday starting at 9:30, and Sundays during the summer

standing start.

occurrence.pattern: Club members also gather each Sunday night at An Spailpín Fánach

events.raw:
> "Established in 1993, the Cork Singers' Club has uniquely featured in every
> Mother Jones festival since the opening night on 31st July 2012. Eagerly
> awaited each year, the Cork Singers' Club will present an evening of songs.
> It has ensured that the tradition of singing remains alive in Cork, no
> instruments are allowed. For locals and visitors this is an opportunity to
> hear songs being sung in a pure manner in front of an attentive audience
> and an opportunity to sing a song themselves. Club members also gather each
> Sunday night at An Spailpín Fánach to hone their remarkable art."

> "Under the Fear An Tí Jim Walsh, the Cork Singers' Club represents the
> unique singing heritage of the people of Cork."
events.summary:
Unaccompanied traditional singing, every Sunday night upstairs at An
Spailpín Fánach — no instruments allowed, Jim Walsh as fear an tí, and the
floor open to anyone who has a song. The club has been keeping this going
since 1993. The season runs October to June and it is dark for the summer.

Wednesdays 5pm – 9pm · Gaelscoil na Dúglaise, Douglas, Cork · Small classes,
Beginner – Advanced · 30 / 60 min · Solo & Ceilí Band

Fiddle • Tin Whistle • Concertina • Bodhrán • Accordion • Flute • Banjo

> "Douglas is a vibrant Branch of Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann. Established
> 28 years ago, from humble beginnings with just a handful of members, the
> branch has continued to grow and prosper. We now have a membership of over
> 300 ranging in age from five to eighty five years old who attend classes
> each Wednesday night in Gaelscoil na Dúglaise in the heart of Douglas
> village, in Cork City."

From `/cost-of-classes/`: "We operate a 2-term system. Term 1: September –
December (12 weeks). Term 2: Mid-January – May (15 weeks)." "Instruments: €9
per class." Membership: "Junior €6, Senior €12, Family €20." "Please note

Four hours of classes every Wednesday evening in a Douglas village
Gaelscoil, across fiddle, whistle, concertina, bodhrán, accordion, flute and
banjo plus song and dance — the largest Comhaltas branch in the city, with
over three hundred members aged five to eighty-five. Registration for the
September term is described as opening shortly.

events.title: Trad session at Sin É

occurrence.pattern: Non-stop traditional music 7 days a week, from 6 to close Monday to Saturday and from 5 on Sunday

events.raw:

events.summary:
Sin É's standing session, every night of the week — the longest-running in
Cork and the one the rest of the city is measured against. Music has been
played here without a break since the 1950s and 60s, when most Cork pubs
had closed their doors to it.
events.description:
The long-established home of Irish traditional music in Cork city, the
Irish words 'Sin é' literally translate to mean 'That's it', in reference
to the funeral parlour located next door. Sin é is widely viewed as the
best traditional pub in Cork!

Non-stop traditional music 7 days a week from 6 – close Monday – Saturday,
and from 5 on Sunday. Music and Drink are the focus but please feel free to
bring some food with you! (hot food not allowed)

Voted one of the best places in the world to spend St Patrick's Day.

Having first opened its doors in 1889, the pub has always been an
intriguing spot – to say the least – and has a very devout and widespread
following of people, patrons that hail from every different sort of
background.

The Sin É doesn't tolerate egos particularly well and respect is shown to
all who show respect to it and its patrons. Roots run deep here, with
generations of families from the locality mixing easily with newcomers and
tourists. The truth is that you can't be a blow in at the Sin é – you
either dig what's going on or you don't.

Traditional music has always been played at the pub, even when it was seen
as uncool in the 1950s, 60s and 70s; and unlike the tourist sessions that
pop up in other pubs during the summer, the Sin É has had live Irish music
every week for over 50 years now. We host a Trad Session 7 nights a week at
7pm – truly a must for any music fan! The best of Irish is always heard
every Tuesday at 9.30pm as well as Fridays and Sundays at 6.30pm, whatever
night of the week you arrive – good music is guaranteed.

The Sin É loves Stout, Horse racing, Cheltenham week, Traditional music,
Reggae (it started in Cork, just ask the bar man!), Rock and Blues,
Conversation, Singing and maintaining folks' hopes and dreams. We're very
much a community, so cross the river Lee and join us!

Oireachtas na Gaeilge award for it, and its walls are lined with Cork Folk
Festival posters going back decades.
events.description:
The Gables has been the recipient of many awards including Oireachtas na
Gaelige music award for pub session. The walls are lined with framed posters
from past Cork Folk Festivals, the history of the music of a city, with some
featured names of those appearing having played the Gables on many
occasions.

The session has been visited by travelling musicians from far and wide with
many diverse cultures. They have been tutored in all forms of music,
classical, jazz, folk and blues but in some way all are drawn to the allure
of traditional Irish music. They are drawn to the allure of the session. The
way in which a group of musicians can gather, some having met only for the
first time, pick a set of random tunes and yet all know exactly when to
start, change and stop, all in perfect unison. Yes the phenomena of the
musical gathering that it 'the session'.

events.title: Tuesday session at Blarney Castle Hotel

occurrence.pattern: Every Tuesday from 9:30 on till around 1:00am

events.raw:
**Blarney Castle Hotel**, The Square, Blarney, Cork. Schedule: Tuesday.

> "Very nice and welcoming session every Tuesday from 9:30 on till around
> 1:00am!!!"

> "Session still going strong after so many years. Still laid-back and
> welcoming (although still fairly energetic tunes). Lots of nice polkas
> and slides since many musicians travel here from the Newmarket/Kanturk
> direction."

> "Confirmed by management (May, 2024), still going on Tuesday nights." —
> 2 years ago, the page's most recent comment.
events.summary:
The only session in this category outside the city, in the hotel bar on
Blarney square, running late into the night. Polkas and slides from the
Newmarket and Kanturk direction rather than a city session.

events.title: Tuesday session at Franciscan Well
events.raw:
**Franciscan Well**, 14b North Mall, Cork. Schedule: Tuesday.

> "I don't know if this is an open session of not, but it's every Tuesday
> at 8:30pm." — 7 years ago

> "Tuesdays at 7:30pm" — 1 year ago

> "We were welcomed when we visited this June. We had been told about it
> the night before by Hughie Kennedy, who plays the box there." — 2 months

events.summary:
A Tuesday session in the North Mall brewpub, confirmed as welcoming by a
visitor two months ago. The start time has drifted in the comments from
8:30 to 7:30; the more recent reading is recorded.

events.title: Monday session at Gaia

occurrence.pattern: Every Monday, during university term only — not on holidays or midterm breaks

events.raw:
**Gaia**, Cork. Schedule: Monday.

> "The session is held by the UCC TradSoc. Therefore, it's mainly
> university students playing, but everyone's welcome. They also learn a
> new set for each session. Happening only during university times, not on
> any holidays or midterm breaks."

> "It's a 7pm start, according to the bar's Facebook page." — 1 year ago,
> the page's most recent comment.
events.summary:
The UCC TradSoc's Monday session — mostly students, a new set learned each
week, and open to anyone. It runs in university term only, so it is dark
for the summer and back with the academic year.

events.title: Saturday afternoon session at Cork City Library
events.raw:
**Cork City Library**, 61 Grand Parade, Cork. Schedule: Saturday.

> "A session every Saturday from 4pm to 5:15pm, organised by Creative
> Tradition: https://www.creativetradition.ie/"

> "Sessions are now from 3:30pm to 5pm. Everyone welcome!" — the most
> recent of the page's two comments.
events.summary:
The one session in the category that is not in a pub: an open Saturday
afternoon session in the city library on Grand Parade, run by Creative
Tradition and explicitly open to anyone.
